body.input: One of the things that inspired the general public,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and just in conversations I have with my parents or something with my mom,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that just loves what was done, is kind of at least the notion

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that there was some display of creativity,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: some new strategies, new behaviors that were created.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: That, again, has echoes of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So is there something that stands out?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Do you see it the same way that there's creativity

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and there's some behaviors, patterns that you saw

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that AlphaZero was able to display that are truly creative?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So let me start by saying that I think we should ask what creativity really means.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So to me, creativity means discovering something which wasn't known before,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: something unexpected, something outside of our norms.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so in that sense, the process of reinforcement learning

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: or the self-play approach that was used by AlphaZero,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: it's the essence of creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: It's really saying at every stage, you're playing according to your current norms,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and you try something, and if it works out, you say,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: hey, here's something great, I'm going to start using that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And then that process, it's like a micro discovery

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that happens millions and millions of times over the course of the algorithm's life,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: where it just discovers some new idea, oh, this pattern is working really well for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: I'm going to start using that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And now, oh, here's this other thing I can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: I can start to connect these stones together in this way,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: or I can start to sacrifice stones or give up on pieces

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: or play shoulder hits on the fifth line or whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: The system's discovering things like this for itself continually, repeatedly all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so it should come as no surprise to us then,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: when if you leave these systems going,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that they discover things that are not known to humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that to the human norms are considered creative.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And we've seen this several times.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: In fact, in AlphaGo Zero, we saw this beautiful timeline of discovery

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: where what we saw was that there are these opening patterns

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that humans play called joseki.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: These are the patterns that humans learn to play in the corners,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and they've been developed and refined over literally thousands of years in the game of Go.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And what we saw was in the course of the training AlphaGo Zero,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: over the course of the 40 days that we trained this system,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: it starts to discover exactly these patterns that human players play.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And over time, we found that all of the joseki that humans played

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: were discovered by the system through this process of self-play

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and this sort of essential notion of creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But what was really interesting was that over time,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: it then starts to discard some of these in favor of its own joseki that humans didn't know about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And it starts to say, oh, well, you thought that the Knights move pincer joseki was a great idea,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: but here's something different you can do there,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: which makes some new variation that humans didn't know about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And actually now the human Go players study the joseki that AlphaGo played,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and they become the new norms that are used in today's top level Go competitions.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: That never gets old.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Even just the first to me, maybe just makes me feel good as a human being

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: that a self-play mechanism that knows nothing about us humans discovers patterns that we humans do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: It's a kind of affirmation that we're doing okay as humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So in this domain and other domains, we figured out it's like the Churchill quote about democracy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: It sucks, but it's the best one we've tried.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So in general, taking a step outside of Go,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and you have like a million accomplishments that have no time to talk about with AlphaStar and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and the current work.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But in general, this self-play mechanism that you've inspired the world with by beating the world champion Go player.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Do you see that as, do you see it being applied in other domains?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Do you have sort of dreams and hopes that is applied in both the simulated environments

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and the constrained environments of games?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Constrained, I mean, AlphaStar really demonstrates that you can remove a lot of the constraints,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: but nevertheless, it's in a digital simulated environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Do you have a hope, a dream that it starts being applied in the robotics environment

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: and maybe even in domains that are safety critical and so on and have a real impact in the real world,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: like autonomous vehicles, for example, which seems like a very far out dream at this point?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So I absolutely do hope and imagine that we will get to the point where ideas just like these are used

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: in all kinds of different domains.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: In fact, one of the most satisfying things as a researcher is when you start to see other people use your algorithms in unexpected ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So in the last couple of years, there have been a couple of nature papers where different teams unbeknownst to us

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: took AlphaZero and applied exactly those same algorithms and ideas to real world problems of huge meaning to society.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So one of them was the problem of chemical synthesis, and they were able to beat the state of the art in finding pathways

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: of how to actually synthesize chemicals, retrochemical synthesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And the second paper actually just came out a couple of weeks ago in Nature showed that in quantum computation,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: one of the big questions is how to understand the nature of the function in quantum computation and a system based on AlphaZero

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: beat the state of the art by quite some distance there again.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So these are just examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And I think the lesson which we've seen elsewhere in machine learning time and time again is that if you make something general,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: it will be used in all kinds of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: You provide a really powerful tool to society and those tools can be used in amazing ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so I think we're just at the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And for sure, I hope that we see all kinds of outcomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So the other side of the question of reinforcement learning framework is, you usually want to specify reward function and objective function.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: What do you think about ideas of intrinsic rewards?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And when we're not really sure about, you know, if we take human beings as existence proof that we don't seem to be operating according to a single reward,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: do you think that there's interesting ideas for when you don't know how to truly specify the reward,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: you know, that there's some flexibility for discovering it intrinsically or so on in the context of reinforcement learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So I think, you know, when we think about intelligence, it's really important to be clear about the problem of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And I think it's clearest to understand that problem in terms of some ultimate goal that we want the system to try and solve for.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And after all, if we don't understand the ultimate purpose of the system, do we really even have a clearly defined problem that we're solving at all?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Now, within that, as with your example for humans, the system may choose to create its own motivations and subgoals that help the system to achieve its ultimate goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And that may indeed be a hugely important mechanism to achieve those ultimate goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But there is still some ultimate goal I think the system needs to be measurable and evaluated against.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And even for humans, I mean, humans, we're incredibly flexible. We feel that we can, you know, any goal that we're given, we feel we can master to some degree.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But if we think of those goals, really, you know, like the goal of being able to pick up an object or the goal of being able to communicate or influence people to do things in a particular way or whatever those goals are,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: really, they are subgoals really that we set ourselves. You know, we choose to pick up the object, we choose to communicate, we choose to influence someone else.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And we choose those because we think it will lead us to something in later on. We think that that's helpful to us to achieve some ultimate goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Now, I don't want to speculate whether or not humans as a system necessarily have a singular overall goal of survival or whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But I think the principle for understanding and implementing intelligence is has to be that if we're trying to understand intelligence or implement our own, there has to be a well defined problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Otherwise, if it's not, I think it's like an admission of defeat that for there to be hope for understanding or implementing intelligence, we have to know what we're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: We have to know what we're asking the system to do. Otherwise, if you don't have a clearly defined purpose, you're not going to get a clearly defined answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: The ridiculous big question that has to naturally follow, because I have to pin you down on this thing, that nevertheless, one of the big silly or big real questions before humans is the meaning of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Is us trying to figure out our own reward function? And you just kind of mentioned that if you want to build intelligence systems, and you know what you're doing, you should be at least cognizant to some degree of what the reward function is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So the natural question is, what do you think is the reward function of human life, the meaning of life for us humans, the meaning of our existence?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: I think I'd be speculating beyond my own expertise, but just for fun, let me do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Yes, please.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And say, I think that there are many levels at which you can understand the system and you can understand something as optimizing for a goal at many levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so you can understand that the, you know, let's start with the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Like, does the universe have a purpose? Well, it feels like it's just at one level, just following certain mechanical laws of physics, and that that's led to the development of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But at another level, you can view it as actually, there's the second law of thermodynamics that says that this is increasing in entropy over time forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And now there's a view that's been developed by certain people at MIT that this you can think of this as as almost like a goal of the universe, that the purpose of the universe is to maximize entropy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So there are multiple levels at which you can understand a system.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: The next level down, you might say, well, if the goal is to is to maximize entropy, well, how do how does how can that be done by a particular system?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And maybe evolution is something that the universe discovered in order in order to kind of dissipate energy as efficiently as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And by the way, I'm borrowing from Max Tegmark for some of these metaphors, the physicist.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But if you can think of evolution as a mechanism for for dispersing energy, then then evolution, you might say, is then becomes a goal, which is if if evolution disperses energy by reproducing as efficiently as possible,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: what's evolution then? Well, it's now got its own goal within that, which is to actually reproduce as effectively as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And now how does reproduction, how is that made as effective as possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Well, you need entities within that that can survive and reproduce as effectively as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so it's natural that in order to achieve that high level goal, those individual organisms discover brains, intelligences, which enable them to support the goals of evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And those brains, what do they do? Well, perhaps the early brains, maybe they were controlling things at some direct level.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Maybe they were the equivalent of pre-programmed systems, which were directly controlling what was going on and setting certain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: things in order to achieve these particular goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But that led to another level of discovery, which was learning systems, you know, parts of the brain which were able to learn for themselves and learn how to to program themselves to achieve any goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And presumably, there are parts of the brain where goals are set to parts of that system and provides this very flexible notion of intelligence that we as humans presumably have,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: which is the ability to kind of why the reason we feel that we can we can we can achieve any goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So so it's a very long winded answer to say that, you know, I think there are many perspectives and many levels at which intelligence can be understood.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And and each of those levels, you can take multiple perspectives.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: You know, you can view the system as something which is optimizing for a goal, which is understanding it at a level by which we can maybe implement it and understand it as AI researchers or computer scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Or you can understand it at the level of the mechanistic thing which is going on, that there are these atoms bouncing around in the brain and they lead to the outcome of that system is not in contradiction with the fact that it's it's also a decision making system that's optimizing for some goal and purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: I've never heard the description of the meaning of life structured so beautifully in layers.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: But you did miss one layer, which is the next step, which you're responsible for, which is creating the the artificial intelligence and the layer on top of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And I can't wait to see.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Well, I may not be around, but I can't wait to see what the next layer beyond that will be.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Well, let's just take that that argument and pursue it to its natural conclusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So the next level indeed is for for how can our how can our learning brain achieve its goals most effectively?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Well, maybe it does so by by us as learning beings building a system which is able to solve for those goals more effectively than we can.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so when we build a system to play the game of go, you know, when I said that I wanted to build a system that can play go better than I can,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: I've enabled myself to achieve that goal of playing go better than I could by by directly playing it and learning it myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And so now a new layer has been created, which is systems which are able to achieve goals for themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: And ultimately, there may be layers beyond that where they set sub goals to parts of their own system in order to to achieve those and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: So credible. So the story of intelligence, I think, I think is is a multi layered one and a multi perspective one.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: We live in an incredible universe, David.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: Thank you so much, first of all, for dreaming of using learning to solve go and building intelligent systems and for actually making it happen and for inspiring millions of people in the process.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

body.input: It's truly an honor. Thank you so much for talking to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Silver: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #86

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: That's not the meaning of my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: So the meaning of my life is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: which is probably different from yours

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: and different from other people's,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: but we each make our own meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: So we set up goals we want to achieve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: we want to write a book, we want to do whatever it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: we do write a quartet, we want to win a football match.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: And these are short-term goals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: well, maybe even quite long-term goals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: which are set up by our brains,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: which have goal-seeking machinery built into them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: But what we feel, we don't feel motivated

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: by the desire to pass on our DNA mostly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: We have other goals, which can be very moving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: They could even be called spiritual in some cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: We want to understand the riddle of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: We want to understand consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: We want to understand how the brain works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: These are all noble goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: Some of them can be noble goals anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: And they are a far cry from the fundamental biological goal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: which is the propagation of DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: But the machinery that enables us to set up these

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: higher level goals is originally programmed into us

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: by natural selection of DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: The propagation of DNA,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: but what do you make of this unfortunate fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: that we are mortal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: Do you ponder your mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: Does it make you sad?

body.input: Does it?

body.input: It makes me sad that I shall have to leave

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: and not see what's going to happen next.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: If there's something frightening about mortality,

body.input: apart from sort of missing, as I've said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: something more deeply, darkly frightening,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: it's the idea of eternity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: But eternity is only frightening if you're there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: Eternity before we were born,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: billions of years before we were born,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: and we were effectively dead before we were born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: As I think it was Mark Twain said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: I was dead for billions of years before I was born

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: and never suffered the smallest inconvenience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: That's how it's going to be after we leave.

body.input: eternity is a frightening prospect.

body.input: is under a general anesthetic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: which is what it'll be.

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words

body.input: because they are never going to be born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: Certainly, those unborn ghosts include greater poets

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: the set of actual people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: In the teeth of these stupefying odds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: it is you and I, in our ordinariness, that are here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: We privileged few who won the lottery

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: of birth against all odds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

body.input: How dare we whine at our inevitable return

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Dawkins: Evolution, Intelligence, Simulation, and Memes | Lex Fridman Podcast #87

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: But I put a lot of stock and certainly have a lot of respect for someone who puts in an honest day's work to do useful things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And just generally to have like not a zero-sum mindset or like have more of a grow the pie mindset.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: If you sort of say like when we see people like perhaps including some very smart people kind of taking an attitude of like doing things that seem like morally questionable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: it's often because they have at a base sort of axiomatic level a zero-sum mindset and they without realizing it, they don't realize they have a zero-sum mindset or at least they don't realize it consciously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And so if you have a zero-sum mindset, then the only way to get ahead is by taking things from others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: If the pie is fixed, then the only way to have more pie is to take someone else's pie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: But this is false. Like obviously the pie has grown dramatically over time, the economic pie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: So in reality, you can have – overuse this analogy – you can have a lot of pie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Pie is not fixed. So you really want to make sure you're not operating without realizing it from a zero-sum mindset where the only way to get ahead is to take things from others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Then that's going to result in you trying to take things from others, which is not good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: It's much better to work on adding to the economic pie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: So creating more than you consume, doing more than you – yeah. So that's a big deal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: I think there's like a fair number of people in finance that do have a bit of a zero-sum mindset.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: I mean, it's all walks of life. I've seen that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: One of the reasons Rogan inspires me is he celebrates others a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: This is not creating a constant competition. There's a scarcity of resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: What happens when you celebrate others and you promote others, the ideas of others, it actually grows that pie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: The resources become less scarce. That applies in a lot of kinds of domains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: It applies in academia where a lot of people see some funding for academic research as zero-sum. It is not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: If you celebrate each other, if you get everybody to be excited about AI, about physics, about mathematics, I think there'll be more and more funding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: I think everybody wins. Yeah, that applies, I think, broadly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Yeah, yeah. Exactly.

body.input: Better engineer?

body.input: That's one of the great ones, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Yeah. Love is a many-splendored thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: I mean, there's, because we've talked about so many inspiring things like be useful in the world, sort of like solve problems, alleviate suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: But it seems like connection between humans is a source, you know, it's a source of joy, it's a source of meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And that's what love is, friendship, love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Now, I just wonder if you think about that kind of thing when you talk about preserving the light of human consciousness and us becoming a multi-planetary species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: I mean, to me at least, that means like if we're just alone and conscious and intelligent, it doesn't mean nearly as much as if we're with others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Right. And there's some magic created when we're together. The friendship of it, and I think the highest form of it is love, which I think broadly is much bigger than just sort of romantic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: But also, yes, romantic love and family and those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Well, I mean, the reason I guess I care about us becoming multi-planet species and a space-faring civilization is foundationally, I love humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And so I wish to see it prosper and do great things and be happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And if I did not love humanity, I would not care about these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: So when you look at the whole of it, the human history, all the people who's ever lived, all the people alive now, it's pretty, we're okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: On the whole, we're a pretty interesting bunch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Yes. All things considered. And I've read a lot of history, including the darkest, worst parts of it. And despite all that, I think on balance, I still love humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: You joked about it with the 42. What do you think is the meaning of this whole thing? Is there a non-numerical representation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Yeah. Well, really, I think what Douglas Adams was saying in Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy is that the universe is the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And what we really need to figure out are what questions to ask about the answer that is the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And that the question is really the hard part. And if you can properly frame the question, then the answer, relatively speaking, is easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: So therefore, if you want to understand what questions to ask about the universe, you want to understand the meaning of life, we need to expand the scope and scale of consciousness so that we're better able to understand the nature of the universe and understand the meaning of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And ultimately, the most important part would be to ask the right question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Thereby elevating the role of the interviewer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Yes, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: As the most important human in the room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: Good questions are, you know, it's hard to come up with good questions. Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: But yeah, it's like that is the foundation of my philosophy is that I am curious about the nature of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And, you know, and obviously I will die, I don't know when I'll die, but I won't live forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: But I would like to know that we are on a path to understanding the nature of the universe and the meaning of life and what questions to ask about the answer that is the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #252

body.input: And so if we expand the scope and scale of humanity and consciousness in general, which includes silicon consciousness, then that seems like a fundamentally good thing.
