body.input: possible, ranging from no symptoms at all

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to this deadly viral pneumonia

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: that's killed so many people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the problem is, if you just count the number of cases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the people who have very few symptoms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: often don't show up for testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They're outside of the can of public health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so it's really hard to know the answer to your question

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: without understanding how many people are infected,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because you can probably tell the number of deaths,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: even though there's some controversy over that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But that, so the numerator is possible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but the denominator is much harder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: How much controversy is there about the death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're gonna go on million tangents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Is that, okay, I have a million questions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: so one, I love data so much,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but I'm like almost tuned out paying attention to COVID data

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because I feel like I'm walking on shaky ground.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't know who to trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Maybe you can comment on different sources of data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: different kinds of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The death one, that seems like a really important one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Can we trust the reported deaths associated with COVID,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: or is it just a giant messy thing that mixed up?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then there's this kind of stories

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: about hospitals being incentivized

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to report a death as COVID death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So there's some truth in some of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Let me just talk about the incentives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In the United States, we passed this CARES Act

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: that was aimed at making sure hospital systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: didn't go bankrupt in the early days of the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: A couple of things they did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: One was they provided incentives to treat COVID patients.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Tens of thousands of dollars

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: extra per COVID patient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the other thing they did is they gave a 20% bump

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to Medicare payments for elderly patients who are treated

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: with COVID, the idea is that there's more expensive

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to treat them at the early days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that did provide incentive to have a lot of COVID patients

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: in the hospital because your financial success

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: of the hospital or at least lack of financial ruin

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: depended on having many COVID patients.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The other thing on the death certificates,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: is that reporting of deaths is a separate issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't know that there's a financial incentive there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but there is this sort of like complicated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: when you fill out a death certificate

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: for a patient with a lot of conditions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: like let's say a patient has diabetes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: a patient that while that diabetes could lead

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to heart failure, you have a heart attack, heart failure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: your lungs fill up, then you get COVID and you die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So what do you write on the death certificate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Was it COVID that killed you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Was it the lungs filling up?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Was it the heart failure?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Was it the diabetes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's really difficult to like disentangle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I think a lot of times what's happened is

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: people have erred on the side of signing it as COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now what's the evidence of this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's been a couple of audits of death certificates

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: in places like Santa Clara County where I live,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: in Alameda County, California,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: where they carefully went through the death certificates

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and said, okay, is this reasonable to say

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: this was actually COVID or was COVID incidental?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And they found that about 25%, 20, 25% of the deaths

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: were more likely incidental than directly due to COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I personally don't get too excited about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, it's a philosophical question, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like ultimately what kills you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Which is an odd thing to say if you're not in medicine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but like really it's almost always multifactorial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's not always just the bus hits you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The bus hits you, you get a brain bleed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Was the brain bleed that killed you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Would it have burst anyway?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The bus hits you, killed you, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The way you die is a philosophical question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but it's also a sociological and psychological question

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because it seems like every single person

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: who has passed away over the past couple of years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: kind of the first question that comes to mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Was it COVID?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Not just because you're trying to be political,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but just in your mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: No, I think there's a psychological reason for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We spent the better part of at least a half century

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: in the United States not worried too much

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: about infectious diseases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The notion was we'd essentially conquered them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It was something that happens in faraway places

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that's true for much of the developed world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Life expectancy were going up for decades and decades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And for the first time in living memory,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: we have a disease that can kill us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I think we're effectively evolved to fear that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like the panic centers of our brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the lizard part of our brain takes over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And our central focus has been avoiding this one risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so it's not surprising that people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: when they're filling out death certificates

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: or thinking about what led to the death,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: this most salient thing that's in the front

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: of everyone's brain would jump to the top.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we can't ignore this very deep psychological thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: when we consider what people say on the internet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: what people say to each other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: what people write in scientific papers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It feels like when COVID has been brought onto this world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: everything changed in the way people feel about each other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: just the way they communicate with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think the level of emotion evolved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think in many people, it brought out the worst in them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: For sometimes short periods of time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: sometimes it was all therapeutic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: like you were waiting to get out the darkest parts of you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: just to say, if you're angry at something in this world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm going to say it now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that's probably talking to some deep primal thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: fear we have for maladies of all different kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then when that fear is aroused and all the deepest emotions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it's like a Freudian psychotherapy session,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but across the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's something that psychologists are going to have a field day

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: with for a generation, trying to understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think what you say is right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but piled on top of that is also this impetus to empathy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to empathize compassion toward others, essentially militarized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm protecting you by some actions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and those actions, if I don't do them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: if you don't do them, well, that must mean you hate me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's created this social tension that I've never seen before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We looked at each other as if we were just simply sources of germs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: rather than people to get to know, people to enjoy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: people to learn from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It colored basically almost every human interaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: for every human on the planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, the basic common humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's like you can wear a mask, you can stand far away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but the love you have for each other when you look into each other's eyes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: that was dissipating by region, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I've experienced, having traveled quite a bit throughout this time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it was really sad, even people that are really close together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: just the way they stood, the way they looked at each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It made me feel for a moment that the fabric that connects all of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: is more fragile than I thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If you walk down the street, or if you did this during COVID,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm sure you had this experience where you walk down the street,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: if you're not wearing a mask, or even if you are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: people would jump off the sidewalk as you walked past them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: as if you're poison, even though the data are that COVID spreads

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: indifferently outdoors, if at all, really, outdoors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But it's not simply a biological or infectious disease phenomenon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: or epidemiological phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It is a change in the way humans treated each other, I hope temporary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I do want to say on the flip side of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: so I was mostly in Boston, Massachusetts when the pandemic broke out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that's where I was, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then I came here to Austin, Texas, to visit my now good friend Joe Rogan,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and he was the first person, without pause,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: this wasn't a political statement, this was anything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: just walked toward me, gave me a big hug, and said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it's great to see you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I can't tell you how great it felt, because I, in that moment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: realized the absence of that connection back in Boston

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: over just a couple of months.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we'll talk about it more, but it's tragic to think about that distancing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: that dissolution of common humanity at scale,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: what kind of impact it has on society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Just across the board, political division,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and just in the quiet of your own mind, in the privacy of your own home,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the depression, the sadness, the loneliness, at least the suicide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And forget suicide, just low-key suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, no, I think that's the suffering, that isolation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're not meant to live alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're not meant to live apart from one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's, of course, the ideology of lockdown,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: is to make people live apart, alone, isolated, so that we don't spread diseases to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But we're not actually designed as a species to live that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that, what you're describing, I think, if everyone's honest with themselves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: have felt, especially in places where lockdowns have been very militantly enforced,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: has felt deep into their core.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, if I could just return to the question of deaths,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: you said that the data isn't perfect because we need these kind of seroprevalence surveys

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to understand how many cases there were to determine the rate of deaths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we need to have a strong footing in the number of deaths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But if we assume that the number of deaths is approximately correct,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: like what's your sense, what kind of statements can we say about the deadliness of COVID

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: across different demographics, maybe not in a political way or in the current way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but when history looks back at this moment of time, 50 years from now, 100 years from now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the way we look at the pandemic 100 years ago, what will they say about the deadliness of COVID?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think the deadliness of COVID depends on not just the virus itself, but who it infects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So probably the most important thing about the deadliness of COVID is this steep age gradient in the mortality rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So according to these seroprevalence studies that have been done, now hundreds of them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: mostly from before vaccination, because vaccination also reduces the mortality risk of COVID,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the seroprevalence studies suggest that the risk of death, if you're say over the age of 70, is very high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You know, 5% if you get COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If you're under the age of 70, it's lower, 0.05, but there's not a single sharp cutoff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's more like I have a rule of thumb that I use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So if you're 50, say the infection fatality rate from COVID is 0.2%, according to the seroprevalence data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: that means 99.8% survival if you're 50.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And for every seven years of age above that, double it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Every seven years of age below that, have it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So a 57-year-old would have a 0.4%, mortality, a 64-year-old would have a 0.8%, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if you have a severe chronic disease like diabetes or if you're morbidly obese, it's like adding seven years to your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And this is for unvaccinated folks?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is unvaccinated before Delta also.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Are there a lot of people that would be listening to this with PhDs at the end of their name that would disagree with the 99.8%, would you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I think there's some disagreement over this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the disagreement is about the quality of the seroprevalence studies that were conducted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So as I said earlier, I was a senior investigator in three different seroprevalence studies very early in the epidemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I view them as very high-quality studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In Santa Clara County, what we did is we used a test kit that we obtained from someone who works in Major League Baseball, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He ordered these test kits very early, in March 2020, that accurately measures antibodies in the bloodstream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: These test kits were eventually approved by the – had an EUA by the Emergency Use Authorization by the FDA shortly after we did this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it had a very low false positive rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: False positive means if you don't have these COVID antibodies in your bloodstream, the kit shows up positive anyways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That turns out to happen about 0.5% of the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And based on studies, a very large number of studies looking at blood from 2018, you try it against this kit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And 0.5% of the time – 2018, there shouldn't be antibodies there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So to COVID, if it turns positive, it's a false positive, 0.5% of the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then, like a false negative rate, about 10%, 12%, something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't remember the exact number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But the false positive rate is the important thing there, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you have a population in March 2020 or April 2020 with very low fraction of patients having been exposed to COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You don't know how much, but low.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Even a small false positive rate could end up biasing your study quite a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But there's a formula to adjust for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You can adjust for the false positive rate, false negative rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We did that adjustment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And those studies found in a community population – so leaving aside people in nursing homes who have a higher death rate from COVID –

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the death rate was 0.2% in Santa Clara County and in LA County.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Across all age groups in the community, meaning just regular folks?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, so that's actually a real important question, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the Santa Clara study, we did this Facebook sampling scheme, which is – I mean, not the ideal thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but it was very difficult to get a random sample during lockdown.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Where we put out an ad on Facebook soliciting people to volunteer for the study, a randomly selected set of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We were hoping to get a random selection of people from Santa Clara County, but the people who tended to volunteer were from the richer parts of the county.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like I had Stanford professors writing, begging to be in the study because they wanted to know their antibody levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So we did some adjustment for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In LA County, we hired a firm that had a pre-existing representative sample of LA County.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But it didn't include nursing homes, it didn't include people in jail, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It didn't include the homeless populations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So it's representative of a community dwelling population, both of those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And there we found that both in LA County and Santa Clara County in April 2020, something like 40 to 50 times more infections than cases in both places.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So for every case that had been reported to the public health authorities, we found 40 or 50 other infections, people with antibodies in their blood, that suggested that they'd had COVID and recovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So people were not reporting, or severe, at least in those days, under reporting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, I mean, there was testing problems. There weren't so many tests available.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: People didn't know. A lot of them, we asked a set of questions about the symptoms they'd faced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And most of them said they faced no symptoms, or at most 30, 40% of them said they faced no symptoms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, even these days, how many people report that they get COVID when they get COVID?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Okay, have those numbers, that 0.2%, has that approximately held up over time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That is. So if Professor John Iannidis, who's a colleague of mine at Stanford, is a world expert in meta-analysis, probably the most cited scientist on Earth, I think, at least living,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: he did a meta-analysis of now 100 or more of these seroprevalence studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And what he found was that that 0.2% is roughly the worldwide number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In fact, I think he cites this lower number, 0.15%, as the median infection fatality rate worldwide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So we did these studies, and it generated an enormous amount of blowback by people who thought that the infection fatality rate is much higher.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And there's some controversy over the quality of some of the other studies that are done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so there are some people who look at this same literature and say, well, the lower quality studies tend to have lower IFRs, the higher quality studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: IFR?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Oh, infection fatality rate, I apologize. I do this in lectures too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I'm going to rudely interrupt you and ask for the basics sometimes, if it's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: No, of course. So these higher quality studies, they say, tend to produce higher IFRs. But the problem is that if you want a global infection fatality rate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: you need to get seroprevalence studies from everywhere, even in places that don't necessarily have the infrastructure set up to produce very, very high quality studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And in poor places in the world, like places like Africa, the infection fatality rate is incredibly low.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And in some richer places, like New York City, the infection fatality rate is much higher.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's a range of IFRs in a single number. This sometimes surprises people because they think, well, it's a virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It should have the same properties no matter where it goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But the virus kills or infects or hurts in interaction with the host.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the properties of both the host and the virus combine to produce the outcome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But you also mentioned the environment too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, I'm thinking mainly just about the person. Like, if I'm going to think about it, like the most simplest way to think about it is age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Age is the single most important risk factor. So older places are going to have a higher IFR than younger places.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Africa, 3% of Africa is over 65. So in some sense, it's not surprising that they have a low infection fatality rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that's one way you would explain the difference between Africa and New York City in terms of the fatality rate is the age, the average age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. And especially in the early days of the epidemic in New York City, the older populations living in nursing homes were differentially infected

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: based on because of policies that were adopted to send COVID-infected patients back to nursing homes to keep hospitals empty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What do you mean by differentially infected?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The policy that you adopt determines who is most exposed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. Okay. So that's what I mean by differentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The policy, it's the person that matters. I mean, it's not like the virus just kind of doesn't care.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, the policy determines the nature of the interaction. There is some contribution from the environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Different regions have different proximity maybe of people interacting or the dynamics of the way they interact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm like if you have situations where there's lots of intergenerational interactions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: then you have a very different risk profile than if you have societies where generations are more separate from one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Okay. So let me just finish real fast about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you have in New York, you have a population that was infected in the early days that was very likely going to die, had a much higher likelihood of dying if infected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so New York City had a higher IFR, especially in the early days than Africa has had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The other thing is treatment. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the treatments that we adopted in the early days of the epidemic, I think actually may have exacerbated the risk of death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Which treatments?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So like using ventilators, like the over-reliance on ventilators is what I'm primarily thinking of, but I can think of other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But that also we've learned over time how better to manage patients with the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you have all those things combined. So that's where the controversy over this number is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, New York City also is a central hub for those who tweet and those who write powerful stories and narratives in article form.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I remember there was quite dramatic stories about sort of doctors in the hospitals and these kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, there's very serious, very dramatic, very tragic deaths going on always in hospitals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Those stories, loved ones losing each other on a deathbed, that's always tragic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you can always write a hell of a good story about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you should about the loss of loved ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But they were doing it pretty, pretty well, I would say, over this kind of dramatic deaths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So in response to that, it's very unpleasant to hear, even to consider the possibility that the death rate is not as high as you might feel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. I was surprised by the reaction, both by regular people and also the scientific community in response to those studies, those early studies in April of 2020.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: To me, they were studies. I mean, they're the kinds of, not exactly the kinds of work I've worked on all my life, but kind of like the kind of, you know, you write a paper and you get responses from your fellow scientists and you change the paper to improve it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You have hopefully learned something from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, but to push back is just a study.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But there are some studies, and this is kind of interesting because I've received similar pushback on other topics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's some studies that if wrong, might have a wide ranging detrimental effects on society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that's the way they would perceive the studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If you say the death rate is lower and you end up, as you often do in science, realizing that, nope, that was a flaw in the way the study was conducted or we're just not representative of a broader population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then you realize the death rate is much higher. That might be very damaging in people's view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that's probably where the scientific community sort of just steel man. The kind of response is that's where they felt like, you know, there's some findings where you better be damn sure before you kind of report them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, I mean, we were pretty sure we were right. And it turns out we were right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So like when we so we released the Santa Clara study via this open science process and this server called Med Archive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's designed for releasing studies that have not yet been peer reviewed in order to garner comment from the scientists before peer review.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The LA County study, we went through the traditional peer review process and got it published in the Journal of American Medical Association sometime in like July, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I forget the date of 2020. The Santa Clara study released in April of 2020 in this sort of working paper archive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The reason was that we felt we had an obligation. We had a result that was we thought was quite important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we wanted to tell the scientific community about it and also tell the world about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it was we wanted to get feedback. I mean, that's part of the purpose of sending it to these kinds of places.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think a lot of the problem is that when people think about published science, they think of it as automatically true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if it goes through peer review, it's automatically true. If it hasn't gone through peer review, it's not automatically true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And especially in medicine, when we're not used to having this access to pre peer reviewed work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, in economics, actually, that's quite normal. You take years to get something published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So there's a very active debate over or discussion about papers before they're peer reviewed in this sort of working paper way, much less normal or much newer in medicine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so I think part of that, the perception about what those that what process happens in open science when you release a study that that got people confused.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you're right. It was a very important result because we had just locked the world down in middle of March.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: With, I think, catastrophic results. And if that study was right, if our study was right, that meant we'd made a mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And not because the death rate was low. That's actually not the key thing there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The key thing is that we had adopted these policies, these test and trace policies, these policies, these lockdown policies aimed at suppressing the virus level to close to zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That was essentially the idea. If we can just get the virus to go away, we won't have to ever worry about it again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The main problem with our result, as far as that strategy was concerned, wasn't the death rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It was the 40 to 50 times more infections than cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It was the two and a half percent or three percent or four percent prevalence rate that we identified of the antibodies in the population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If that number is right, it's too late. The virus is not going to go to zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And no matter how much we test and trace and isolate, we're not going to get the viral level down to zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So we're going to have to let the virus go through the entire population in some way or some other way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We can talk about that in a bit. That's the Great Barrington Declaration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You don't have to let the virus go through the population. You can shield preferentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The policy we chose was to shield preferentially the laptop class, the set of people who could work from home without losing their job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we did a very good job at protecting them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, let me take a small tangent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're going to jump around in time, which I think will be the best way to tell the story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that was the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. OK, actually, can I go back one more thing for that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because that's really important and I should have I should have started with this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What led me to do those studies was a paper that I had remembered seeing from the H1N1 flu epidemic in 2009.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is where I've been much less active in writing about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I had written up like a paper or two about that in 2009.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There there was actually the same debate over the mortality rate, except it unfolded over the course of three years, two or three years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The early studies of the mortality rate in H1N1 counted the number of cases in the denominator, kind of the number of deaths in the numerator,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: cases meaning people identified as having H1N1 showing up, the doctor tested to have it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the earliest estimates of H1N1 mortality were like four percent, three percent, really, really high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Over the course of a couple of more years, a whole bunch of seroprevalence studies, seroprevalence studies of H1N1 flu came out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it turned out that there were a hundred or more times people infected per case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so the mortality rate was actually something like point oh two percent for H1N1, not the three, three, like a hundredfold difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So this made you think, OK, it took us a couple of two or three years to discover the truth behind the actual infections for H1N1.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then what's the truth here and can we get there faster?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. And it spreads in a similar way as the H1N1 flu did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, it spreads via solidization, via person to person breathing, kind of contact up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And maybe some by film eyes, but it seems like that's less likely now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In any case, it seemed really important to me to speed up the process of having those seroprevalence studies so we can better understand who was at risk and what the right strategy ought to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This might be a good place to kind of compare influenza, the flu and COVID in the context of the discussion we just had, which is how deadly is COVID?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you mentioned COVID is a very particular kind of steepness where the x-axis is age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So in that context, could you maybe compare influenza and COVID?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because a lot of people outside of the folks who suggest that the the lizards who run the world have completely fabricated and invented COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Outside of those folks, kind of the natural process by which you dismiss the threat of COVID is say, well, it's just like the flu.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The flu is a very serious thing, actually. So in that comparison, where does COVID stand?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, the flu is a very serious thing. It kills 50,000, 60,000 people a year, something like that, depending on the particular strain that goes around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's in the United States. The primary difference to me, there's lots of differences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but one of the most salient differences is the age gradient and mortality risk for the flu.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the flu is more deadly for two children than COVID is. There's no controversy about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Children, thank God, have much less severe reactions to COVID infection than they do to flu infections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And rate of fatalities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Rate of fatality, all of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think you mentioned, I mean, it's interesting to maybe also comment on, I think in another conversation you mentioned,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: there's a U shape to the flu curve. So meaning like, there's actually quite a large number of kids that die from flu.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. I mean, the 1918 flu, the H1N1 flu, the Spanish flu in the US killed millions of younger people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that is not the case with COVID. More than, I'm going to get the number wrong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but something like 70, 80% of the deaths are people over the age of 60.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We've talked about the fear the whole time, really. But my interaction with folks, now I want to have a family,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I want to have kids, but I don't have that real firsthand experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But my interaction with folks is at the core of fear that folks had is for their children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like that somehow, you know, I don't want to get infected because of the kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like, because God forbid something happens to the kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I think that obviously that makes a lot of sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This kind of the kids come first, no matter what, that's the more priority.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But for this particular virus, that reasoning was not grounded in data, it seems like, or that emotion and feeling was not grounded in data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It wasn't. At the same time, this is way more deadly than the flu just overall, and especially to older people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right? So the numbers, when the story is all said and done, COVID would take many more lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. So, I mean, point two sounds like a small number, but it's not a small number worldwide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What do you think that number will be by the, you know, that's not like, but would we cross, I think it's in the United States,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it's the way the deaths are currently reported, it's like 800,000, something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Do you think we'll cross a million?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Seems likely. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Do you think it's something that might continue with different variants? What?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, I think, so we can talk about the end state of COVID. The end state of COVID is it's here forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that there is good evidence of immunity after infection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: such that you're protected both against reinfection and also against severe disease upon reinfection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the second time you get it, it's not true for everyone, but for many people, the second time you get it will be milder, much milder than the first time you get it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: With the long tail, like that lasts for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. So just there are studies that follow, of course, people who were infected for a year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the reinfection rate is something like somewhere between 0.3 and 1%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And like a pretty fantastic study out of Italy found that there's one in Sweden, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's a few studies have found that similar things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the reinfections tend to produce much milder disease, much less likely to end up in the hospital, much less likely to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So what the end state of COVID is, it's circulating the population forever and you get it multiple times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. And then there's, I think, studies and discussions like the best protection would be to get it and then also to get vaccinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then a lot of people push back against that for the obvious reasons from both sides because somehow the discourse has become less scientific and more political.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, I think you want to, the first time you meet it is going to be the most deadly for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so the first time you meet it, it's just wise to be vaccinated. The vaccine reduces severe disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. Well, we'll talk about the vaccine because I want to make sure I address it carefully and properly and in full context.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But yes, sort of to add to the context, a lot of the fascinating discussions we're having is in the early days of COVID and now for people who are unvaccinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's where the interesting story is. The policy story, the sociological story and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But let me go to something really fascinating just because of the people involved, the human beings involved and because of how deeply I care about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: science and also kindness, respect and love and human things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Francis Collins wrote a letter in October 2020 to Anthony Fauci.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think somebody else. I have the letter, it's not a letter, email, I apologize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Hi, Tony and Cliff. CGBdeclaration.org.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This proposal, this is the Great Barrington Declaration that you're a co-author on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This proposal from the three fringe epidemiologists who met with the secretary seem to be getting a lot of attention and even a co-signature from Nobel Prize winner Mike Levitt at Stanford.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There needs to be a quick and devastating published takedown of its premises.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't see anything like that online yet. Is it underway? Francis Collins, director of the NIH, somebody I talked to on this podcast recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Okay, a million questions I want to ask. But first, how did that make you feel when you first saw this email come to light? When did it come to light?
