metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This week actually, I think or last week.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Okay, so this is because of freedom of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Which by the way, sort of maybe because I do want to add positive stuff on the side of the Francis here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Boy, when I see stuff like that, I wonder if all my emails leaked. How much embarrassing stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like I think I'm a good person, but I haven't read my old emails. Maybe I'm pretty sure sometimes I could be an asshole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, I mean, look, he's a Christian and I'm a Christian. I'm supposed to forgive, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I think he was looking at this Great Barrington Declaration as a political problem to be solved as opposed to a serious alternative approach to the epidemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So maybe we'll talk about it in more detail, but just in case people are not familiar, Great Barrington Declaration was a document that you co-authored that basically argues against this idea of lockdown as a solution to COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you propose another solution that we'll talk about. But the point is, it's not that dramatic of a document.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It is just a document that criticizes one policy solution that was proposed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But it was the policy solution that had been put forward by Dr. Collins and by Tony Fauci and a few other scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I think a relatively small number of scientists and epidemiologists in charge of the advice given to governments worldwide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it was a challenge to that policy that said that, look, there is an alternate path that the path we've chosen, this path of lockdown with an aim to suppress the virus to zero effectively, I mean, that was unstated, cannot work and is causing catastrophic harm to large numbers of poor and vulnerable people worldwide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We put this out in October 4th, I think of 2020, and it went viral. I mean, I've never actually been involved with anything like this, where I just put the document on the web and tens of thousands of doctors signed on, hundreds of thousands of regular people signed on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It really struck a chord of people because I think even by October 2020, people had this sense that there was something really wrong with the COVID policy that we've been following.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And they were looking for reasonable people to give an alternative. I mean, we're not arguing that COVID isn't a serious thing. I mean, it is a very serious thing. This is why we had a policy that aimed at addressing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We were saying that the policy we're following is not the right one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So how does a democratic government deal with that challenge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So to me that, you asked me how I felt. I was actually frankly just, I suspected there had been some email exchanges like that, not necessarily from Francis Collins, around the government around this time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I felt the full brunt of a propaganda campaign almost immediately after we published it, where newspapers mischaracterized it in the same way over and over and over again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And sought to characterize me as sort of a marginal fringe figure or whatnot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And Sunetra Gupta, Martin Kuhl-Dorf, or the tens of thousands of other people that signed it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I felt the brunt of that all year long. So to see this in black and white, in the handwriting essentially, I mean the metaphorical handwriting of Francis Collins was actually frankly a disappointment because I've looked up to him for years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, I've looked up to him as well. I mean, I look for the best in people and I still look up to him. What troubles me is several things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The reason I said about the asshole emails I send late at night is I can understand this email. It's fear, it's panic, not being sure. The fringe, three fringe epidemiologists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Plus Mike Levitt who won a Nobel Prize. I mean. But using fringe, maybe in my private thoughts, I have said things like that about others, like a little bit too unkind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like you don't really mean it. Now add to that, he recently this week or whatever, doubled down on the fringe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is really troubling to me that I can excuse this email, but the arrogance there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That Francis honestly, I mean, broke my heart a little bit there. This was an opportunity to like, especially at this stage, to say, just like I told him, to say I was wrong to use those words in that email.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I was wrong to not be open to ideas. I still believe that this is not like say, like actually argue with the proposal, with the policy of the post solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Also, the devastating published take devastating take down devastating take down. As you say, somebody who's sitting on billions of dollars that they're giving to scientists, some of whom are often not their best human beings because they're fighting with each other over money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Not being cognizant of the fact that you're challenging the integrity, you're corrupting the integrity of scientists by allocating the money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You're now playing with that by saying devastating take down. Where do you think the published take down will come from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It will come from those scientists to whom you're giving money. What kind of example would they give to the academic community that thrives on freedom?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like this, this is, I believe Francis Collins is a great man. One of the things I was troubled by is the negative response to him from people that don't understand the positive impact that NIH had on society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: How many people has helped, but this is exactly the so he's not just a scientist. He's not just a bureaucrat who distributes money. He's also scientific leader that in a time in difficult times we live in is supposed to inspire us with trust, with love, with the freedom of thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He's supposed to, you know those fringe epidemiologists, those are the heroes of science. When you look at the long arc of history, we love those people. We love ideas even when they get proven wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's what always attracted me to science. Like somebody, the lone voice saying, oh no, the moon of Jupiter does move.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, you know, but the funny thing is, you know, Galileo is saying something truly revolutionary. We were saying that what we propose in the Great Barrierton Declaration was actually just the old pandemic plan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It wasn't anything really fundamentally novel. In fact, there were plans like this that lockdown scientists had written in late February, early March of 2020.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So we were not saying anything radical. We were just calling for a debate effectively over the existing lockdown policy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And this is a disappointment, a really truly a big disappointment because by doing this, you were absolutely right Lex. He sent a signal to so many other scientists to just stay silent, even if you had reservations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, devastating takedown. The people, you know how many people wrote to me privately like Stanford, MIT, how amazing the conversation with Francis Collins was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's a kind of admiration because, okay, how do I put it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: A lot of people get into science because they want to help the world. They get excited by the ideas and they really are working hard to help in whatever the discipline is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then there is sources of funding which help you do help at a larger scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you admire those the people that are distributing the money because they're often, at least on the surface, are really also good people. Oftentimes they're great scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So like it's amazing. That's why I'm sort of like sometimes people from outside think academia is broken some kind of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: No, it's a beautiful thing. It really is a beautiful thing. And that's why it's so deeply heartbreaking with this person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't think this is malevolence. I think he's just incompetent in communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Twice. I think there's also arrogance at the bottom of it too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: All of us have arrogance at the bottom. Yes, but there's a particular kind of arrogance. So here it's the same kind of arrogance that you see when Tony Fauci gets on TV and says that if you criticize me, you're not simply criticizing a man, you're criticizing science itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That is at the heart also of this email.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the certainty that the policies that they were recommending, Collins and Fauci were recommending to the President of the United States were right, not just right, but right so far right that any challenge whatsoever to it is dangerous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I think that that is really the heart of that email. It's this idea that my position is unchallengeable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now to be completely, to be as charitable as I can be to this, I believe they thought that. I believe some of them still think that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That there was only one true policy possible in response to COVID. Every other policy was immoral.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if you come from that position, then you write an email like that. You go on TV, you say effectively, la science c'est moi.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. I mean, that is what happens when you have this sort of unchallengeable arrogance that the policy you're following is correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, when we wrote the Great Bank Declaration, what I was hoping for was a discussion about how to protect the vulnerable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, that was the key idea to me and the whole thing was better protection of the older population who really at really serious risk if infected with COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we had been doing a very poor job, I thought, to date in many places in protecting the vulnerable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And what I wanted was a discussion by local public health about better methods, better policies to protect the vulnerable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So when I was what we were met with instead, a series of essentially propagandist lies about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that so much since I kept hearing from reporters in those days, why do you want to let the virus rip? Let it rip. Let it rip.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The words let it rip does not appear in the Great Barrington Declaration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The goal isn't to let the virus rip. The goal is to protect the vulnerable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Let society go as open schools and do other things that function as best it can in the midst of a terrible pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes, but not let the virus rip where the most vulnerable aren't protected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The goal was to protect the vulnerable. So why let it rip?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because it was a propaganda term to hit the fear centers of people's brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Oh, these people are immoral. They just want to let the virus go through society and hurt everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That was that was that was the idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It was a way to preclude a discussion and preclude a debate about the existing policy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I have this app called Clubhouse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Anyway, it's a great way to talk to regular people in Russian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The whole thing was like theater to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I haven't thoroughly researched, but looking at the resume, they were like pretty solid researchers and doctors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And they were mocking everybody who was at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, it doesn't matter what they stood for, but they were just mocking people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the arrogance was overwhelming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I had to shut off because I couldn't handle that human beings can be like this to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then I went back to just to double check, is this really how many people are here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then as I open my mouth, I say, thank you so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I said, I'm worried that the kind of arrogance with which things are being discussed here will further divide us, not unite us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They said to me, enough of that nonsense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You're bringing on French epidemiologists also. Yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But this broke my heart, the arrogance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And this is echoes of that arrogance is something you see in this email.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I really would love to have a million things to talk about to try to figure out how can we find a path forward?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think a lot of a lot of the problems we've seen in the discussion over COVID, especially in the scientific community,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: there's two ways to look at science, I think, that have been competing with each other for a while now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: One way, and this is the way that I view science and why I've always found it so attractive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: is an invitation to a structured discussion where the discussion is tempered by evidence, by data, by reasoning and logic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So it's a dialectical process where if I believe A and you believe B, well, we talk about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: we come up with an experiment that distinguishes between the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And while B turns out to be right, I'm all frustrated, but I buy you dinner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I say, no, no, no, no, C. And then we go on from there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's what science is at its best, is this process of using data in discussion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's a human activity to have the truth unfold itself before us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: On the other hand, there's another way that people have used science or thought about science as truth in and of itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If it's science, therefore it's true automatically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And what does the science say to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, the science never says to do anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The science says, here's what's true, and then we have to apply our human values to say, OK, well, if we do this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: then this is likely to happen. That's what the science says.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If we do that, then that is likely to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, we'd rather have this than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But does science tell us that we'd rather have this than that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Does our human values tell us that we'd rather have this than that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Science plays a role, but it's not the only thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's not the only role.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It helps us understand the constraints we face, but it doesn't tell us what to do in the face of those constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But underneath it, at the individual level, at the institutional level, it seems like arrogance is really destructive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the flip side of that, the productive thing is humility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So sort of always not being sure that you're right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is actually kind of a show. Russell talks about this for AI research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, the question I have here for you is this this email so clearly captures some maybe echo, but maybe a core to the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the NIH. So I've had two decades of NIH funding. I've sat on NIH review panels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The purpose of the NIH is what you said earlier, Lex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So and the way you do that is you say, OK, we're going to put, you know, 50 million dollars on the research in Alzheimer's disease this year or 70 million dollars on HIV or whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So it's essentially an endeavor to support the work of scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the final results being so surprisingly high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So good, right. Yeah. And so the but the problem then was normally it would take a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The FDA would tell Pfizer to go back and try it in this subgroup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They'd work more on dosing. They do all all these kinds of things that kind of didn't we really didn't have time for in the middle of the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you have a you have a basis for approval that it's less full than normally you would have for a population scale vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But the results were good. The results looked really good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And actually, I should say, for the most part, that's been borne out when we've given the vaccine at scale in terms of protection against severe disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. Right. So people who have got the vaccine for a very long time after they had the full vaccination have had great protection against going being hospitalized and dying if they get covid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Let's separate because this seems to be there's critics of both categories, but different kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And kids and old not older people like, let's say, five years old and above or something like that, or 13 years old and above.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So for those, it seems like the reduction of the rate of fatalities and serious illness seems to be something like 10x.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, for older people, it is a godsend.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This vaccine, it transforms the problem of focus protection from something that's quite challenging possible, I believe, but quite challenging to something that's much, much more manageable because the vaccine in and of itself, when deployed in older populations is a form of focus protection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes, well, by the way, we'll talk about the focus protection in one segment because it's such a brilliant idea for this pandemic of future pandemics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I thought the sociological psychological discussion about the letter from Francis Collins is because it was so recent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It has been so troubling to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I'm glad we talked about that first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But so there seems to be the vaccines work to reduce deaths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that has especially the most transformative effects for the older.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So can I let me give you, I've told you one thing that I got wrong in the pandemic. Let me tell you the second thing I got wrong for sure in the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In January of this year, 2021, I thought that the vaccines would stop infection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. It would make it so that you were much less likely to be infected at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because the antibodies that were produced by the vaccines looked like they are neutralizing antibodies that would essentially block you from being infected at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That turned out to be wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. So I think it became clear as data came out from Israel, which vaccinated very early, that they were seeing surges of infection, even in a very highly vaccinated population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That the vaccine does not stop infection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you're a used car salesman and you're selling the vaccine and the features you thought a vaccine would have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I have a similar kind of sense when the vaccine came out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Vaccine would reduce if you somehow were able to get it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It would reduce rate of death and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But it would also reduce the chance of you getting it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if you do get it, the chance of you transmitting it to somebody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it turns out that those latter two things are not as definitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Or in fact, I mean, I don't know to what degree they're not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think it's a little complicated because I think the first two or three months after you're fully vaccinated, after the second dose, you have 60, 70 percent efficacy peak against infection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that which is pretty good, right. But by six, seven, eight months, that drops to 20 percent. Some places, some studies like there's a study out of Sweden suggested might even drop to zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But and then you're also infectious for some period of time if you do get it, even though you're vaccinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Although there seems to be lucidated that the period of time you're infectious is shorter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's shorter, but the infectivity per day is about as high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you still it's the point is that that the vaccine might reduce some risk of infecting others, but it's not a categorical difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So unvaccinated, it's not safe to be in the presence of just vaccinated people. You can still get infected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. So, I mean, there's a million things I want to ask here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But is there in some sense because the vaccine really helps on the worst part of this pandemic, which is killing people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Doesn't that mean where does the vaccine hesitancy come from in terms of it seems like obviously a vaccine is a powerful solution to let us open this thing up?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes, I wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed with Sunetra Gupta in December of last year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: A very night with a very naive title which says we can end the lockdowns in a month.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the idea was very simple. Vaccinate all vulnerable people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then open up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Open up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. And the idea was that the lockdown harms is related.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is directly related to the Great Barrierton Declaration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The Great Barrierton Declaration said the lockdown harms are devastating to the population at large.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's this considerable segment of people that are vulnerable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Protect them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, with the vaccine, we have a perfect tool to protect the vulnerable, which is I still believe, I mean, is true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. You vaccinate the vulnerable, the older population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And as you said, it's a tenfold decrease in the mortality risk from getting infected, which is, I mean, amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that was the strategy we outlined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What happened is that the vaccine debate got transformed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So first, you're asking about vaccine hesitancy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think first there's the inherent limitations of how to measure vaccine safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. So we talked a little bit about the trial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But also after the trial, there's a mechanism, and this is the work I've been involved with before COVID,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: on tracking and identifying and checking whether the vaccines actually are safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the central challenge is one of causality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you no longer have the randomized trial, but you want to know, is the vaccine, when it's deployed at scale, causing adverse events?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, you can't just look at people who are vaccinated and see what adverse events happen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because you don't know what would have happened if the person had not been vaccinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you have to have some control group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now, what happened is there's several systems to check this that the CDC uses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: One very, very commonly known one now is called VAERS, the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There, anyone who has an adverse event, either a regular person or a doctor, can just go report.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Look, I had the vaccine, and two days later, I had a headache or whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The person died a day after that, the vaccine, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now, the vaccine was rolled out to older people first, and older people die sometimes, with or without the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So sometimes you'll see someone's vaccinated, and a few days later, they die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Did the vaccine cause it or something else cause it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's really difficult to tell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In order to tell, you need a control group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: For that, there are other systems the FDA and CDC have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's one called VSD, Vaccine Safety Data Link.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's another system called BEST.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I forget what the acronym is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Essentially, to track cohorts of people vaccinated versus unvaccinated with as careful a matching as you can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's not randomized, and C, if you have safety signals that pop up in the vaccinated relative to the control group unvaccinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's, for instance, how the myocarditis risk was picked up, especially in young men.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's also how the higher risk of blood clots in middle-aged and older women with the J&J vaccine was picked up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There, what you have are situations where the baseline risk of these outcomes are so low that if you see them in the vaccinated arm at all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it's not hard to understand that the vaccine did this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Young men should not be having myocarditis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Middle-aged women should not be having huge blood clots in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: When you see that, you can say it's linked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The rates are low.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Young men, maybe one in 5,000, one in 10,000 of the vaccine-related myocarditis, pericarditis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Middle-aged women, I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm not sure what the right number might be, but I'd say it's one in hundreds of thousands, something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: These are rare outcomes, but they are vaccine-linked outcomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: How do you deal with that as a messaging thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think you just tell people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You tell people here are the risks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You transparently tell them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They're not getting into something that they don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Don't treat people like they're children and need to be told lies because they won't understand the full complexity of the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: People, I think, are pretty good at...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Or actually, people with time are good at understanding data, but better than anything, they're extremely good at detecting arrogance and bullshit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you give them either one of those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'll give you one that's where I think it's greatly undermined the demand for the vaccine is this weird denial that if you recover from COVID, you have extremely good immunity, both against infection and access to the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that denial leads to people distrusting the message given by the CDC director, for instance, in favor of the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Why would you deny a thing that's such an obvious fact?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You can look at the data and it just pops out at you that people that are COVID recovered are not getting affected again at very high rates, much lower rates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: After these kinds of conversations, I'm sure after this very conversation, I often get a number of messages from Joe Rogan and from Sam Harris, who to me are people I admire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think are really intelligent, thoughtful human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They also have a platform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I believe, at least in my mind, about this COVID set of topics, they represent a group of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Each group has smart, thoughtful, well-intentioned human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I don't know who is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But I do know that they're kind of tribal a little bit, those groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so the question I want to ask is, what do you think about these two groups and this kind of tension over the vaccine that sometimes just keeps finding different topics on which to focus on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: like whether kids should get vaccinated or not, whether there should be vaccine mandates or not, which seem to be often very kind of specific policy kinds of questions that miss the bigger picture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think it's a symptom of the distrust that people have in public health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think this kind of schism over the vaccine does not happen in places where the public health authorities have been much more trustworthy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you don't see this vaccine has been seen in Sweden, for instance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What's happened in the United States is the vaccine has become, first because of politics, but then also because of the scientific arrogance, this sort of touchstone issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And people line up on both sides of it. And the different language you're hearing is structured around that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So before the election, for instance, I did a testimony in the House on measurement of vaccine safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I was invited by the Republicans. There were, I think, four other experts invited by the Democrats or three other experts invited by the Democrats, each of whom had a lot of experience in measuring vaccine safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I was really surprised to hear them each doubt whether the FDA would do a reasonable job in assessing vaccine safety, including by people who have long records of working with the FDA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, these are professionals, great scientists whose main goal in life is to make sure that unsafe vaccines don't get released into the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if they are, they get pulled. And they're casting doubt on the vaccine, the ability to track vaccine safety before the election.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then after the election, the rhetoric switched on a dime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: All of a sudden, it's Republicans that are cast as if they're vaccine and hesitant. That kind of political shift, the public notices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If all it takes is an election to change how people talk about the safety of the vaccine, well, we're not talking science anymore, many people think, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that created its hesitancy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The other thing I think the hesitancy, some politicians viewed it as a political opportunity to demonize people who are hesitant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that itself fueled hesitancy, right? If you're telling me I'm a rube that just doesn't want the vaccine because I want everyone to die, well, I'm going to react really negatively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if you're talking down to me about my legitimate concerns about whether this vaccine is safe to take, I've heard from women who are thinking about getting pregnant, should I take the vaccine? I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, there are all kinds of questions, legitimate questions that I think should have good data to answer that we don't necessarily have good data to answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So what do you do in the face of that? Well, one reaction is to pretend like we know for a fact that it's safe when we don't have the data to know for a fact in that particular group with that particular set of clinical circumstances, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that I think breeds hesitancy. People can detect that bullshit. Whereas if you just tell people, you know, I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, lead with humility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, you will end up with a better result.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Let me ask you about, I've recently had a conversation with the Pfizer CEO.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is part therapy session, part advice, because again, I really want us to get through this together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it feels like the division is a thing that prevents us from getting through this together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And once again, just like with Francis Collins, a lot of people wrote to me, words of support, and a lot of people wrote to me words of criticism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm trying to understand the nature of the criticism. So some of the criticism had to do with against the vaccine and those kinds of things that I have a better understanding of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But some kind of deep distrust of Pfizer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So actually looking at Big Pharma broadly, I'm trying to understand, am I so naive that I just don't see it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because, yes, there's corrupt people and they they're greedy, they're flawed in all walks of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But companies do quite an incredible job of taking a good idea to scale and making some money with that idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But they are the ones that achieve scale on a good idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't know. It's not obvious to me. I don't see where the manipulation is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the fear that people have and I talked to Joe about this quite a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think this is a legitimate fear and a fear you should often have that money has influence, this proportional influence, especially in politics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the fear is that the policy of the vaccine was connected to the fact that lots of money could be made by manufacturing the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I understand that. And it's actually quite a heck of a difficult task to alleviate that concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like you really have to be a great man or woman or leader to convince people that you're not full of shit, that you're not just playing a game on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't know. It's a difficult task. But at the same time, I really don't like the natural distrust every billionaire distrust everybody who's trying to make money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because it feels like under a capitalistic system, at least the way to do a lot of good, like to do good at scale in the world is by being at least in part motivated by profit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I share your ambivalence. So on the one hand, you have a fantastic achievement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You have the discovery of the vaccine and then the manufacturing at scale so that billions of people can take the vaccine in a relatively short time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That is a remarkable achievement that could not have happened without companies like Pfizer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: On the other hand, there is this sort of corrupting influence of that money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Just to give you one example, there's an enormous controversy over whether relatively inexpensive repurposed drugs can be used to treat the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: None of no company like Pfizer has any interest whatsoever in evaluating it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Even Merck, I think it was Merck that had the patent on ivermectin now expired, has no interest at all in checking to see if it works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Not only do they not have interest, they have a way of talking about people who might have a little bit of interest that's again full of arrogance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that is what troubles me. It's back to the play of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They're not a bit of curiosity. One, the natural curiosity of a human being that should always be there and an open mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And second, in the case of ivermectin and other things like that, you have to acknowledge that there's a very large number of people who care about this topic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And this is a way to inspire them to also play in the space of science, to inspire them with science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You can't just dismiss everybody. You can't just dismiss people, period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. Well, I mean, I think here, take ivermectin. There's actually a study funded by the NIH, by Tony Fauci's NIAID and the NIH called ACTIV-6 that's a randomized trial of ivermectin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's due to be completed in March 2023.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So normally when you have private actors like these big drug companies that have no interest in conducting some kind of scientific experiment that would have some public benefit,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it's the job of the government, and in this case, the NIH, to fund that kind of work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The NIH has been incredibly slow in its evaluations of these repurposed drugs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it's been left to lots of other private activities of uneven quality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And hence, that's why you have these big fights. Because the data are not solid, you're going to have these big fights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. But also, okay, forget the process of science here, the studies, not enough effort being put into the studies, just the way it's being communicated about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, no, like horse paste. I mean, come on. The FDA put a tweet out telling people who are like, they're taking ivermectin because they've heard good things about it and they're sick and they're desperate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And to call it horse paste was just, that was terrible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That was deeply irresponsible. My hope is grounded in the fact that young people see the bullshit of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Young PhD students, graduate students, young students in college, they see the less than stellar way that our scientific leaders and our political leaders are behaving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and then the new generation will not repeat the mistakes of the past. That is my hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because that's the cool thing I see about young people is they're good at detecting bullshit and they don't want to be part of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's my hope in the space of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Let me return to this idea of the Great Barrington Declaration. Return to the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So what are the basics? Can you describe what the Great Barrington Declaration is? What are some of the ideas in it? You mentioned focus protection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What are your concerns about lockdowns? Just paint the picture of this early proposal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Sure. So the Great Barrington Declaration, first, why is it called Great Barrington Declaration?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's such a great name. It's such an epic name, but the reason why it's called that is way less than epic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It was because the conference, which is organized by Martin Kulldorf, who was a professor at Harvard University, by a statistician,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: he actually designed the safety system, the statistical system that the FDA uses for tracking vaccine safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He and I had met previously just the summer before that summer, and he invited me to come to this small conference

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: where he was inviting me and Sunetra Gupta, who was a professor of theoretical epidemiology at Oxford University.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I jumped at the chance because I knew that Martin and Sunetra were both smarter than me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and it would be fun to talk about what the right strategy would be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: On the drive in, I didn't know what the name of the town was, and I asked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They said it was Great Barrington, and I had it in the back of my head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Martin and I arrived a little early, and we were writing an op-ed about some of the ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: hopefully we'll get to talk about very soon, about focus protection and the right strategy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And when Sunetra arrived, we realized we'd actually come basically to the same place about the right way to deal with the epidemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I thought, well, why don't we write something like the Port Huron Statement?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That was what I had in the back of my head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I'm like, well, what's the name of this town again? It was Great Barrington.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, so it's not Barrington. It's Great Barrington.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Which is fantastic, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's so over the top that it's perfect. It's literally like the Big Bang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's something about these over the top fun titles that just really deliver the power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's my main contribution, the title, the name Great Barrington Decor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But yeah, so it was kind of a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the idea is actually, while the title is great, and I think that it was written in a very stylish way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: it's less than a page. You can go look online and read it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's written for, not for scientists, but for the general public so that people can understand the ideas really simply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But it is not actually a radical set of ideas. It actually represents the old pandemic plans

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: that we've used for a century dealing with other similar pandemics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it's twofold. First, let me talk about the science it rests on, and then I'll talk about the plan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The science actually, some of it we already talked about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's this massive age gradient in the risk of COVID infection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Older people face much higher risk than younger people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The second bit of science is all... That's not controversial, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Even if you think the IFR is 0.7 or 0.2, no matter what, everyone agrees on this age gradient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The second bit of science is also not controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The lockdown-focused policies that we followed have absolutely devastating consequences on the health of the population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Let me just give you some examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This was known in October of 2020 when we wrote it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the UN was sounding alarms that there would be tens of millions of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: who would starve as a consequence of the economic dislocation caused by the lockdowns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that's come to pass.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Hundreds of thousands of children in places like South Asia dead from starvation as a consequence of lockdowns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The priorities like the treatment of patients with tuberculosis in poor countries stopped because of lockdowns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Childhood vaccinations of measles, mumps, rubella, DPT, diphtheria, so on, pertussis, tetanus,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: all those standard vaccination campaigns stopped.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Tens of millions of children skipping these doses for diseases that are actually deadly for them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Is there, just on a small tangent, is it well understood to you what are the mechanisms that stop all those things because of lockdowns?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Is it some aspect of supply chain? Is it just literally because hospital doors are closed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Is it because there's a disincentive to go outside by people even when they deeply need help?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's all of the above.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But a lot of those efforts, especially those vaccination efforts, are funded and run by Western efforts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like Gavi is a, I think it's a Gates-funded thing actually, that provides vaccines for millions of kids worldwide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And those efforts were scaled back. Malaria prevention efforts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254
