body.input: So in the developing world, it was a devastating effect, these lockdowns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There was also direct effects, like in India, the lockdowns, when they first instituted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: there was an order that 10 million migrant workers who live in big cities and they live hand-to-mouth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: they buy coconuts, they sell the coconuts with the money, they buy food for themselves and coconuts for the next day to sell,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: walk back to their villages or go back to their villages overnight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So 10 million people walking back to their villages or taking a train back, a thousand died en route,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: overcrowded trains, dying essentially on the side of the road. I mean, it was absolutely inhumane policy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the lockdowns there, it's actually, it's kind of like what's happened in the West as well, but it was so severe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There was a zero prevalence study done in Mumbai by a friend of mine at the University of Chicago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And what he found was that in the slums of Mumbai, there were 70% zero prevalence in July or August of 2020,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: whereas in the rest of Mumbai was 20%. So it was incredibly unequal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The lockdowns protected the relatively well-off and spread the disease among the poor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that's in the developing world. In the developed world, the health effects of lockdowns were also quite bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. So we've talked already about isolation and depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There was a study done in July of 2020 that found that one in four young adults seriously considered suicide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now, suicide rates haven't spiked up so much,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but the depths of despair that would lead somebody to seriously consider suicide itself should be a source of great concern in public health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, this is one of the troubling things about measuring well-being is we're okay at measuring death and suicide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're not so good at measuring suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's like people talk about maybe even Holladamore under Stalin or the concentration camps with Hitler.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We talk about deaths, but we don't talk about the suffering over periods of years by people living in fear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: by people starving, psychological trauma that lasts a lifetime, all of those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, and just to get back to that point, we closed schools, especially in blue states, we closed schools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now, richer parents could send their kids to private schools, many of which stayed open even in the blue states.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They could get pods, they could get tutors, but that's not true for poor and middle-class parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And as a result, what we did is we took away life opportunities for kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We tried to teach five-year-olds to read via Zoom in kindergarten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the consequence actually, you think, okay, we can just make it up, but it's really difficult to make that up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's a literature in health economics that shows that even relatively small disruptions in schooling

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: can have lifelong consequences, negative consequences for kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So they end up growing up poorer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They lead shorter lives and less healthy lives as a consequence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that's what the literature now shows is likely to happen with the interruptions of schooling that we had in the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Many European countries actually managed to avoid this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There were in the early days of the epidemic great indications that children first were not very severely at risk from COVID itself, nor are they super spreaders.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Schools were not the source of community spread. Communities spread the disease to schools, not the other way around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we can talk about the scientific basis of that if you'd like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But that was pretty well known even in October.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We closed hospitals in order to keep them available to COVID patients.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But as a result, women skipped breast cancer screening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: As a result, they are showing up with late stage breast cancer that should have been picked up last year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Men and women skipped colon cancer screening, again, with later stage disease that should have been picked up last year with earlier stage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: For patients with diabetes, it's very important to have regular screening for blood sugar levels and sort of counseling for lifestyle improvement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we skipped that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: People stayed home with heart attacks and died at home with heart attacks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you had this like sort of wide range of medical and psychological harms that were being utterly ignored as a result of the lockdowns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Plus there's the economic pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So like you said, the whatever is a good term for the non laptop class, people would lose their jobs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There might be in the Western world support for them financially, but the big loss there that is perhaps correlated with depression and suicide is loss of meaning, loss of hope for the future, loss of kind of a sense of stability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: All the pride you have in being able to make money that allows you to pave your own way in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And yes, just having less money than you're used to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So your family, your kids are suffering, all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's a there's a again, economics literature on this on deaths of despair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It was called 2009.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There was the Great Recession.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It led to an enormous uptake in overdose from drugs, suicidality, depression as a result of the job losses that happened during the Great Recession.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, that's happening again, like an enormous increase in drug overdoses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's not that's not an accident.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's a lockdown harm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. Same same thing with with the job losses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The job losses, by the way, are like it's so interesting because the states that stayed open have had much, much lower unemployment than the states that stayed closed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The labor force participation rates declined by three percent. It's women that separated because they stayed home with their kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We've reversed a generation of women when improving women's participation in the labor force.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Do you think it has to do with institutions that we mentioned that there was so much priority given or so much power given to maybe NIH versus other civilian leaders?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Or do people just not care about the economic pain, the leaders?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, because to me, it was obvious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, probably it's just studying history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Whenever I listen to people on Twitter, on mainstream news or just anything, I realize that's the very kind of top.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The people that have a voice represent a tiny selection of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so whenever there's hard times, I always kind of think about the quiet, the voiceless, the quiet suffering of the tens of millions of the hundreds of millions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Do political leaders not just give a damn?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I think it was actually a very odd ethical thing at the beginning of the pandemic where if you brought up economic harms at all, you were seen as callous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I had a reporter call me up almost at the very beginning of the epidemic asking me about a very particular phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So he was anticipating a rise in child abuse because children were going to be staying at home, child abuse is generally picked up at school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that actually happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the reported child abuse dropped, but actual child abuse increased because normally you pick up the child abuse at school and you have the intervention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So yeah, I sort of started talking about, well, there's going to be some economic harms and they're going to have health consequences, but the economic harms matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But he counseled me and I think he had my best interests at heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Like if you were to put that in the story, I would be essentially be canceled because the narrative that arose in March of 2020 is if you care about money at all, you're evil and crass.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You must only care about lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The problem with that narrative is that that money, which we're talking about is actually lives of poor people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: When you throw a hundred million people around the world into poverty, you're going to see enormous harm to their health, enormous increases in their mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It is not immoral to think about that and worry about that in the context of this pandemic response.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Our mind focused so much on COVID that it forgot that there are so many other public health priorities as well that need our attention desperately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And this is the thing I sensed about San Francisco when I visited, I was thinking of moving there for a startup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is the thing I'm really afraid of, especially if I have any effect on the world through a startup is losing touch in this kind of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That you mentioned the laptop class living in this world where you're only concerned about this particular class of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And also, you know, perhaps early on in the pandemic amongst the laptop class, there was a legitimate concern for health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You're not sure how deadly this virus is. You're not sure who to listen to. So there's a real concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And then at a certain point when the data starts coming in, you start becoming more and more detached from the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You don't start caring less and less. And you start just swimming in the space of narratives, like existing the space of narratives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you have this narrative in San Francisco, in the laptop class, that you just are very proud that you know the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You're the sole possessors of the truth. You congratulate yourself on it and you don't care what actually gigantic detrimental effect that has on society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because you're mostly fine. I'm so terrified of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, I think the antidote to that is just to remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't think you remember where you came from and remember who you're doing this for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The back of your head should always be what's the purpose? Like, why am I here? What's the purpose of this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And if the purpose is simply self-aggrandizement, then you should rethink because it will just end up being a hollow life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: All of us will be forgotten in the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Focus protection. The idea, the policy. What is focus protection?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. So I was saying that there's two scientific bases, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So one is this steep age gradient and the second is the existence of locked arms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Again, I think there's very little disagreement in the scientific community about both of those facts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If you put those facts together, the obvious policy is to protect the people who are at the most severe risk from the disease itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that's the idea of focus protection. That's the general principle of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The actual implementation of it depends on the living circumstances of the people that are at risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The resources that are available in the community, the technology that's available to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so it's almost always going to be, in fact, it'll always be a local thing because it'll depend on all of those things, which are all local in nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So one very, very obvious thing in a country like ours where so many older people live in institutionalized settings, in nursing home settings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and that's where older, really vulnerable, chronically ill patients often live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And you know this disease affects that group, like most commonly, it is absolutely vital to protect that group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We should have known that in February 2020 from just from the Chinese data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And we should have thought about that group as the key constraint in our policymaking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Instead, we thought about in February and March 2020 as hospital beds as the key constraint.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Hospital beds and ventilator shortages. And so we ran around trying to address that constraint, like a linear programming problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You figure out which constraints binding and you address that one thing and then you go on to the next one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If that one constraint, we said, okay, the constraint is hospital beds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That led to the decision in many of the Northeast states to send COVID infected patients who were on the verge of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: or looked like they were about to recover back to nursing homes, who then spread the disease all through there because they wanted to preserve the hospital beds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, for somebody who loves numerical optimization, I love the way you frame this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But those are kind of connected, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If you actually focus on protecting the vulnerable, you will also have the effect of not hitting the ceiling of the available hospital beds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's the irony. If we protected the vulnerable, the vulnerable are the most likely to be hospitalized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so by protecting the vulnerable, we would also have addressed the shortage of hospital beds more effectively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So that little shift in priority would have had a big impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Okay, but specifically the idea is to, and we could talk about different ideas of how to actually do this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but you basically do a lockdown or something like that on a very small set of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You may have to do that if it's community spread is very high, but generally I think it would depend on, again, the living circumstances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So for instance, if you are in a, if you have a, here's a very simple idea that doesn't require a lockdown forced on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't actually generally not in favor of that kind of forced lockdown because you just won't get cooperation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But what you could do is provide resources to that group of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So imagine you live next door to somebody, an older couple, and there's high community spread.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, they have to go grocery shopping. We did like some of these, some communities did these like senior only grocery hour, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But they have to still have to go out and they might get exposed when they're shopping amongst other seniors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, why not organized home delivery of groceries to them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We did that for the laptop class, right? Or we can even just as a volunteer effort, you know, the older people living next door, just call them up and say, can I help you go out and go shopping for you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so you would have potentially federal support of that kind of thing. So these kinds of efforts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Identify where the vulnerable people live. It's really challenging in multi-generational homes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: LA County, for instance, there's a lot of older people living together with younger people in relatively crowded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There, it's really quite a challenge. But there again, you can use resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So if grandma is worried that grandson has come home, but is potentially being exposed, grandson calls grandma says, I mean, I might've been in a party where I might do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Where COVID was grandma calls public health, public health and says, OK, you can have this hotel room for a couple of days until you check to turn negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In case it wasn't clear, the idea of focus protection is the people that are vulnerable, protect them and everybody else goes on with their lives, open up the economy, just do as it was before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And there was still fear abroad. So there still would be some restrictions people would pose on themselves. They probably would go to parties less. The grandsons probably wouldn't go so many parties, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There would be less participation in big gatherings. You may even say like big gatherings in order to restrict community spread again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm not against any of that. But you shouldn't be closing businesses. You shouldn't be closing churches and synagogues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You shouldn't be forcing people to not go to school. You should not be shuttering businesses. You should just allow society to go on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Some disease will spread. But as we've seen, the lockdown didn't stop the disease from spreading anyways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. So what do you make of the criticism that this idea, like all good ideas, cannot actually be implemented in a heterogeneous society where there's a lot of people intermixing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And once you open it up, people like the younger people will just forget that this is even existing and they'll stop caring about the older people and mess up the whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the government will not want to fund any kind of the great efforts you're talking about about food delivery and then the food delivery services.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Be like, why the heck am I helping out on this anyway? Because like it's not making me much money. And so therefore, like all good ideas, it will collapse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That might be true. I mean, I think it's always a risk with policy thinking. But I think back to the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We actually felt like we were in this together to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Right. I think that that empathy that we had that was used to like tell people to stay in and like happily, not go in happily, but like stay in to like wear a mask or to do all these things that we thought would help other people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: could have been redirected to actually helping the people who most needed to be especially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I do remember March. So this is even way before Barrington, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: March, April, May. There was a feeling like if we all just work together, we'll solve this right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that may be started to when did that start breaking down? I mean, the unfortunately, the election is mixed into this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That became politicized. But I think it lasted quite a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think into the summer, I think there was some of that sense. I don't know. They obviously varied among different people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But I think that it's true. It would have been challenging. It's also true that it's heterogeneous, exactly the way you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But what that means is you need a local response, a response. So like my vision of a public health officer is someone that understands their community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Not necessarily the nation at large, but their community and then works within their community to figure out how to deploy the resources that they have available to do the kind of protection policies we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's what should have happened. Instead, they spent a huge amount of efforts closing, making sure businesses stayed closed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Businesses that, I mean, there are hardware stores that closed. What good did closing a hardware store do for the spread of COVID? If it had an effect on spread, COVID spread, I mean, it's going to be checking to make sure that plexiglass was put up everywhere, which now in retrospect turns out to probably made the disease worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You know, masking enforcement, so shaming around masks. I mean, a huge amount of effort on things that were only tangentially related to focus protection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What if we turned our energy, that enormous energy put into that instead into focus protection of the vulnerable? That's essentially the conversation I was calling for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And it wasn't, I mean, I didn't think of it as we had every single idea. I mean, we gave some concrete proposals and we got, but the criticism we got was that those concrete proposals weren't enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the answer to that I have is that's true. They weren't enough. I wasn't thinking of them as enough. I was thinking that they would, I wanted to involve an enormous number of people in local public health to help think about how to do focus protection in their communities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The question that's interesting here is about the future too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So COVID has very specific characteristics, like you mentioned about the curve of the death rate based on the, like it seems like with COVID, it's a little bit easier to actually identify a group of people that you need to protect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So other viruses may not be this way. So might lockdown be a good idea, like hardcore lockdown for a future virus that's 10 times deadlier, but spreads at the same rate as COVID?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Or maybe another way to ask that is imagine a virus that's 10 times deadlier. What's the right response?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, I think it's always going to be focus protection, but the group that needs the focus protection may change depending on the biology of the virus. Right? So the polio epidemic in the forties and fifties in the US, the great, the people at most risk were children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We didn't know really at the beginning there was this fecal oral spread. And so we did all kinds of crazy things, including like spraying DDT in communities, which was somehow supposed to get rid of polio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But the focus was on whenever there was an outbreak, they would close the school down. And that was the right thing to do because that group that needed protection was children and the disease was spread, we thought, in schools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I don't think there's a single formula that works, but there's a single principle that works. Right? No matter, I can't, it's hard to imagine a disease that's uniformly deadly across every group and every single person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There's always going to be some group that's differentially harmed. There's always going to be some group that's differentially protected. And that may change over time. Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So like in this disease, in this epidemic, as people got infected and recovered, we now had a class of people that were pretty well protected against the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They should be, instead of ostracizing them because they don't want a vaccine, we should be allowing them to work. I mean, we're having staffing shortages in hospitals now because we forgot that principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's quite a bit of this technology problem. So being able to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: How much of it is a sociological problem? How much of it is a technology problem? Like, where do you put the blame sort of on why this didn't go so great and how it can go great in the beginning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I mean, think about lockdowns. Like, if we didn't have Zoom, we wouldn't have lockdowns. There's a reason in 2009 we didn't lock down. I mean, we didn't have the technology to replace work with this remote technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So we had good lockdown technology in Zoom. We didn't have good focus protection technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. I mean, focus protection is always going to be complicated, especially for something like this that spreads so easily, it's going to be complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I'm the last person to say it would have been perfect. There would have been people that would have gotten sick, but they got sick anyways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The hope was that if we suppress community spread low enough, we can protect the vulnerable. That was the hope by lockdown.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The reality was that only a certain class of people were able to benefit from lockdown. The rest of society, we called them essential workers, had to keep working, and they got sick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And the disease kept spreading. It didn't actually have a substantial effect on community spread in non-laptop class populations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And also, we should probably expand the class of people we call vulnerable to those who would suffer, who have the capacity to suffer, given the policies that you're weighing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's very disingenuous to call the vulnerable just the people. Obviously, we had very specific meaning, but broadly speaking, vulnerable should include anybody who can suffer based on the policies you take in response to a virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That principle you just said is I completely agree with is something I think has been lost and unfortunately lost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the policies themselves, if they have harm, those are real, and we shouldn't pretend like they're not and essentially demonize the people that suffer them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: A lot of times, the depression that we've been talking about, that's thought of as not so important, but it is important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And especially the harm to the people in poor countries, it's like being out of sight, out of mind in much of the rich parts of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Once again, I've hoped that we seeing this, learning the lessons of history with the communication tools we have now will learn this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's like going to another country and bombing targeted terrorist locations, and there's going to be some civilians who die,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: pretending that the child who watches their dad die is not going to grow up, first of all, traumatized,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but second of all, potentially bring more hate to the world than the hate that you were allegedly fighting in the first place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's another sort of considering only one kind of harm and not the full range of harms that are being caused by your policies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You know, like the return to focus protection, we still should be following the policy now for COVID, and we're not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So the vaccines, there's a great shortage in vaccines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You wouldn't know it in the United States and the rich parts of the world, but there's a great shortage of vaccines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're not going to be able to vaccinate most of the entire set of elderly, at least, or larger groups until late 2022.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Huge numbers of older people around the world in poor countries that have not COVID recovered yet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: so they're still quite vulnerable, have not had the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And yet we're talking about vaccinating five-year-olds who benefit, if at all, from the vaccines of just a very little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because they face such a low risk of harm from COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Well, something that's a little bit near and dear to our specific, the two of our hearts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you're at Stanford. So Stanford recently announced that they're going back to virtual, at least for some period of time

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: in response to the escalated, maybe you can clarify, but I think it's in response to the escalated, how would they phrase it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's related to Omicron. And a few other universities are kind of like considering back and forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In my perspective, as somebody who loves in-person lectures, who sees the value of that to students, to young minds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: also looking at the data seems the risk aversion in university policies around this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: given how healthy the student population is, seems not well calibrated, let's put it this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Also, pathological is one way to put it, given that, depending on the university,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but I think many universities require that the student body is vaccinated at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I think it's a big mistake by Stanford to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I'd like to say that because I just hope MIT doesn't, but what are your thoughts about Stanford?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I agree with you. I completely agree with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think we have failed in our mission to educate our students by this decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I think I frankly, just more broadly, I think we failed generally over the course of the last year and a half

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: in living up to our educational mission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In-person teaching is vital.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now, I can understand, you have older faculty, the principle of focus protection says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: provide some alternative teaching arrangements for them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That makes sense to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: From the kid's point of view, they're more harmed by not getting the education we promised them than by COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So applying this principle of this focus protection, let young professors teach in-person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This is before the vaccine. After the vaccine, let everyone teach in-person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah, this is the part I don't understand the discussion we're even having because,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: okay, let's leave focus protection aside here because that's a brilliant policy for perhaps for the future when there's no vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Now with the vaccine, I'm misunderstanding something here because we're now in a space that's psychological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's no longer about biology because with the booster shots, which I believe MIT is now requiring before January,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: with the booster shots, the data shows no matter how old you are, the risks are very low for ending up in a hospital.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Relative to all the other risks you face when you're older, I don't understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Can you explain the policy around closing a university, but also just a policy about just being so scared still in the university setting?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think the great universities have done great harm by modeling this kind of behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yes. To me, sorry to keep interrupting, but to me, the university should be the beacon of great behavior,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: not the beacon of scared conservative, let's not mess up, let's not make it pathological, let's not make anybody angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It should be a place to play in the space of ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think the central problem is actually related to the central problem of COVID policy more generally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The goal seems to be to stop the disease from spreading rather than to reduce the harm from the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: If the goal is to stop disease from spreading, the sad fact is we have no technology to accomplish that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: At this point, because it's already deeply integrated into the human civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's here forever. There's a sero survey of white-tailed deer in the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It turns out 80% of white-tailed deer in the US have COVID antibodies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Dogs get it, cats get it. There's almost certainly human animal transmission of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I've heard bats get it apparently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You have a situation where you have this disease that's here to stay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The vaccines don't stop the spread of it. The lockdowns don't stop the spread of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We have no technology to stop the spread of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're burning the earth trying to do something that's impossible rather than working on what's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Letting regular college happen, that's a great good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Universities are a wonderful invention and it's contributed so much to society to decide to shut it down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The universities should be fighting tooth and nail to not be shut down, not the other way around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Whatever the mechanisms that results in the universities doing that, that's probably me talking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It probably has to do with certain incentives for the administration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It probably has to do with lawyers and legal kinds of things to avoid legal trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Once again, it's when the administration has too much power and too much definition of what the policy is for the university, that's when you get into trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The beauty, the power of the university should be about the faculty and the students.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Administration just gets in the way, get out of the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They can help organize things. They play some important role.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They certainly do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: They need to remember what the mission is. The mission is not safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The mission, actually, universities should be dangerous places for ideas and whatnot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What is the role of fear in a pandemic? We've been dancing around it. Is it useful? Is it destructive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Or is there a complicated story here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because they've taken us back into January 2020, there was so much uncertainty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This could have been a pandemic that is Black Death, the bubonic plague.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It could have killed hundreds of millions of people. We don't know that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're very new to this. It's been a while. We're rusty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: There is some value to fear so that you don't do the stupid thing. You don't just go on living.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I guess where I come from, I think it's almost entirely counterproductive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think fear should never be used as a tactic to manipulate human behavior by public health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The fear on the individual level, that feeling of fear, you should be very hesitant about that feeling

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because it could be easily manipulated by the powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Exactly. I think that fear is natural.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's not something that you have to stoke to get when the facts on the ground suggest it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In fact, the tendency for humans in the face of threats from infectious disease is to exaggerate the fear in their own minds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: of being contaminated by the environment and by others. That's just natural to humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The role of public health is not necessarily to eradicate the fear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Obviously, technological advances can help eradicate the fear, but it's really to help manage that fear

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: and help people put the incentives that come out of that to useful things as opposed to harmful things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What's happened in this pandemic is that there's been a deliberate policy to stoke the fear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: to help make people think that the disease is worse than it actually is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: In survey after survey, you see this. That's been incredibly damaging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Young people have readily given away their willingness to participate in regular life

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: because A, they fear COVID more than they ought, and B, they fear that they're going to harm the vulnerable in their lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You put those two together and you get this powerful demand for lockdowns. You see this all over the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Broadly speaking, you have a powerful demand for irrational policies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I would like to mention the flip side of that. I've been saddened to see how much money there is to be made by the martyrs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: the people, the conspiracy theorists that tell you, you should be afraid of the government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You should be afraid of the man. It feels like fear is the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think there's some guy that once said something about we should fear fear itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He was a president or something. I vaguely remember that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'm worried about both sides here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think the general principle is that should not be a tool of public policy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The public policy should attempt, and public health policy in particular, should attempt to address that fear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's not that you should tell people lies. Of course not. Tell people accurately what the risk is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Give people tools that have evidence that they can address their risk with and level with people when we don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that is the right adult way to deal with this pandemic from a public health point of view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And that is not the policy we have followed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Instead, public health has intentionally stoked the fear in order to gain compliance with this edicts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And I think the consequence of that is people distrust public health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What you're talking about, the distrust of government, I think is partly a consequence of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That movement, which is much smaller once upon a time, is much larger now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because of essentially people look at what public health has done and say, they've lied to me a whole bunch of times and a whole bunch of things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: is the general sense. And there are consequences to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We're going to have to work in public health for a long time to try to regain the trust of the public.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Throughout all of this, you've been inspiring to me, to a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You've been fearless, bold in these kinds of challenging the policies, and not in a martyr kind of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because you're walking the line gracefully and beautifully, I would say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And looking at that, I think you're an inspiration to a lot of young people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I have to ask, what advice would you give them if they're thinking of going into science, if they're thinking of having an impact in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What advice would you give them about their career and maybe about their life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Thinking about somebody in high school, maybe in undergraduate college.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'd say a few things. One is, this is a wonderful profession.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You have an opportunity to improve the lives of so many and do it by having fun, the kind of play we're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's an absolute privilege to be able to work in this kind of area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And to young people looking that have some gifts or desire for this area, I say, please, go for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So this area of science broadly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Yeah. I don't have any gifts in AI, but it could be your, or in health or in medicine or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Whatever your gifts lie, develop them, work hard and develop them, because it's worth it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Not just because you get some status, but because the journey is fun and the result is improvement to the lives of so many.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So I think that is the encouragement I give.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I'd also say, if you're looking at this ugliness of this debate that's happened over the pandemic, I'd say to young people, we need you to come in and help transform it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Many of the people we've seen in this debate that behave poorly, I ask you forgive them. I've done my best to try.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because many of them are acting out of their own sense that they need to do good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: But the mistake they've made is in this arrogance and this power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: When you come in, remember that example as a negative example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And so when you join the debate, you'll join it in a spirit of humility, in a spirit of trying to learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: While keeping that love that led you to enter the field in the first place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: And yeah, choose forgiveness versus derision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The people that you know have messed up, give them a pass.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Because it feels like that's how improvement starts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Honey, I've been thinking this. I told you I'm Christian, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So God has given me many opportunities to forgive people. Learn to practice how to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Gave you a gift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's a very humbling thing, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Is there a memory from when you were young that was very formative to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So you just gave advice to some young people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Is there something that stands out to you that a decision you made, an event that happened, that made you the man you are today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I actually grew up in a relatively poor environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I was born in India and moved when I was four.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: My dad had eight brothers and sisters and my mom had four brothers and sisters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: She grew up in the slum in Calcutta.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: His dad died when he was young and he supported his family, his brothers and sisters with university scholarship money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I came to the US and my dad worked in a McDonald's even though he was an electrical engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Couldn't find a job in 1971.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So we worked at McDonald's.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: We lived in a housing development in Cambridge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: This middle building on the 17th floor, this housing development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that was transformative for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I didn't realize so much at the time how that experience of being essentially poor, lower middle class, what effect it had on my outlook.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You mentioned to me offline that you listened to a conversation that I had with my dad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What impact did your dad have on your life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: What memories do you have about him?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He was a rocket scientist actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He helped design rocket guidance systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: He died when I was 20 and I still miss him to this day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I think that experience of seeing him sacrifice himself for his family, a brilliant man,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: but in many ways frustrated with his opportunities in the world, partly what led him to come to the US in the first place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: That's had a transformative effect on me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I wish I could tell him that looking back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Do you think about your own mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Do you think about your death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Your dad is no longer with us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: You're the old wise sage that represents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It's funny that I've only worried about death once in this pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: Although I had two of my cousins who were 73 and my uncle who was 74 die in India during the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I grieve them, both from COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: The fear of COVID really hit me only really once during this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: It wasn't for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: I recognize it's irrational.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: On the eve of the Santa Clara County zero prevalence study, it was a really interesting thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254

body.input: So many people volunteered to help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay Bhattacharya: The Case Against Lockdowns | Lex Fridman Podcast #254
