body.input: So data augmentation, I mean, first data augmentation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: is the idea of artificially increasing the size

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of your training set by distorting the images

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that you have in ways that don't change

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: the nature of the image, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So you take, you do endless,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: you can do data augmentation on endless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And people have done this since the 1990s, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You take an endless digit and you shift it a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: or you change the size or rotate it, skew it, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You know, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Add noise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Add noise, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it works better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: If you train a supervised classifier with augmented data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: you're gonna get better results.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now it's become really interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: over the last couple of years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: because a lot of self-supervised learning techniques

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: to pre-train vision systems are based on data augmentation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And the basic techniques is originally inspired

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: by techniques that I worked on in the early 90s

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and Jeff Hinton worked on also in the early 90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: They were sort of parallel work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I used to call this Siamese networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So basically you take two identical copies

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of the same network, they share the same weights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And you show two different views of the same object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Either those two different views may have been obtained

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: by data augmentation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: or maybe it's two different views of the same scene

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: from a camera that you moved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: or at different times or something like that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Or two pictures of the same person, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And then you train this neural net,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: those two identical copies of this neural net,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: to produce an output representation, a vector,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: in such a way that the representation for those two images

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: are as close to each other as possible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: as identical to each other as possible, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because you want the system to basically learn a function

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that will be invariant, that will not change,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: whose output will not change

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: when you transform those inputs in those particular ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So that's easy to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: What's complicated is how do you make sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that when you show two images that are different,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: the system will produce different things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because if you don't have a specific provision for this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: the system will just ignore the inputs when you train it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It will end up ignoring the input

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and just produce a constant vector

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that is the same for every input, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That's called a collapse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now, how do you avoid collapse?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So there's two ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: One idea that I proposed in the early 90s

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: with my colleagues at Bell Labs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Jane Bromley and a couple other people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: which we now call contrastive learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: which is to have negative examples, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So you have pairs of images that you know are different

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and you show them to the network and those two copies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and then you push the two output vectors away from each other

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and it will eventually guarantee

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that things that are semantically similar

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: produce similar representations

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and things that are different

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: produce different representations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: We actually came up with this idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: for a project of doing signature verification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So we would collect signatures

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: from multiple signatures on the same person

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and then train a neural net

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: to produce the same representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and then force the system to produce different representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: for different signatures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: This was actually the problem was proposed by people

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: from what was a subsidiary of AT&T at the time called NCR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And they were interested in storing representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of the signature on the 80 bytes

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of the magnetic strip of a credit card.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So we came up with this idea of having a neural net

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: with 80 outputs that we would quantize on bytes

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: so that we could encode the signature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And that encoding was then used to compare

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: whether the signature matches or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So then you would sign, it would run through the neural net

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and then you would compare the output vector

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: to whatever is stored on your card.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Did it actually work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It worked, but they ended up not using it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because nobody cares actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, the American financial payment system

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: is incredibly lax in that respect

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: compared to Europe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Oh, with the signatures?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: What's the purpose of signatures anyway?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Nobody looks at them, nobody cares.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So that's contrastive learning, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So you need positive and negative pairs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And the problem with that is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: even though I had the original paper on this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I'm actually not very positive about it

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: because it doesn't work in high dimension.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: If your representation is high dimensional,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: there's just too many ways for two things to be different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And so you would need lots and lots

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and lots of negative pairs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So there is a particular implementation of this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: which is relatively recent

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: from actually the Google Toronto group,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: where Jeff Hinton is the senior member there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's called SimClear, S-I-M-C-L-R.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's basically a particular way

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of implementing this idea of contrastive learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: the particular objective function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now, what I'm much more enthusiastic about these days

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: is non-contrastive methods.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So other ways to guarantee that

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: the representations would be different

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: for different inputs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's actually based on an idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that Jeff Hinton proposed in the early 90s

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: with his student at the time, Sue Becker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's based on the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of maximizing the mutual information

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: between the outputs of the two systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You only show positive pairs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You only show pairs of images that you know

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: are somewhat similar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And you train the two networks to be informative,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: but also to be as informative of each other as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So basically one representation has to be predictable

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: from the other, essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And he proposed that idea,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: had a couple of papers in the early 90s,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: and then nothing was done about it for decades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And I kind of revived this idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: together with my postdocs at FAIR,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: particularly a postdoc called Stefan Donny,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: who is now a junior professor in Finland at University of Aalto.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: We came up with something that we called Barlow Twins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's a particular way of maximizing

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: the information content of the two systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And we used a vector using some hypotheses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And we have kind of another version of it

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that's more recent now called VicREG, V-I-C-R-E-G.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That means variance, invariance, covariance, regularization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's the thing I'm the most excited about

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: in machine learning in the last 15 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, I'm really, really excited about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: What kind of data augmentation is useful

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: for that non-contrastive learning method?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Are we talking about, does that not matter that much?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It seems like a very important part of the step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: How you generate the images that are similar,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: but sufficiently different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, that's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It's an important step and it's also an annoying step

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: because you need to have that knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: of what data augmentation you can do

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: that do not change the nature of the object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And so the standard scenario,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: which a lot of people working in this area are using,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: is you use the type of distortion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That includes a bunch of people at DeepMind, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Oh, interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I haven't actually touched base with the DeepMind folks, but some of it, Elon or Demisasavvas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, sometimes in your role, you have to kind of create deadlines that are nearer than farther away to kind of create an urgency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because you have to believe the impossible is possible in order to accomplish it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And there's, of course, a flip side to that coin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But it's a weird... you can't be too cynical if you want to get something done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Absolutely. I agree with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But you have to inspire people to work on sort of ambitious things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So, you know, it's certainly a lot harder than we believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But there's no question in my mind that this will happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And now, you know, people are kind of worried about what does that mean for humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: They are going to be brought down from their pedestal, you know, a bunch of notches with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And, you know, is that going to be good or bad?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, it's just going to give more power, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It's an amplifier for human intelligence, really.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So speaking of doing cool, ambitious things, FAIR, the Facebook AI research group, has recently celebrated its eighth birthday.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Or maybe you can correct me on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Looking back, what has been the successes, the failures, the lessons learned from the eight years of FAIR?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And maybe you can also give context of where does the newly minted meta AI fit into, how does it relate to FAIR?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Right. So let me tell you a bit about the organization of all this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, FAIR was created almost exactly eight years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It wasn't called FAIR yet. It took that name a few months later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And at the time I joined Facebook, there was a group called the AI group that had about 12 engineers and a few scientists, like, you know, 10 engineers and two scientists or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I ran it for three and a half years as a director.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I hired the first few scientists and kind of set up the culture and organized it, you know, explained to the Facebook leadership what fundamental research was about and how it can work within industry and how it needs to be open and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And I think it's been an unqualified success in the sense that FAIR has simultaneously produced top level research and advanced the science and the technology, provided tools, open source tools like PyTorch and many others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But at the same time has had a direct or mostly indirect impact on Facebook at the time, now Meta, in the sense that a lot of systems that Meta is built around now are based on research projects that started at FAIR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So if you were to take out deep learning out of Facebook services now and Meta more generally, I mean, the company would literally crumble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, it's completely built around AI these days. And it's really essential to the operations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So what happened after three and a half years is that I changed role. I became chief scientist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So I'm not doing day to day management of FAIR anymore. I'm more of a kind of think about strategy and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And I carry my I conduct my own research. I have my own kind of research group working on self supervised learning and things like this, which I didn't have time to do when I was director.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So now FAIR is run by Joel Pinault and Antoine Borde together because FAIR is kind of split in two now. There's something called FAIR Labs, which is sort of bottom up, science driven research and FAIR Excel, which is slightly more organized for bigger projects that require a little more kind of focus and more engineering support and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So Joel needs FAIR Lab and Antoine Borde needs FAIR Excel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Where are they located?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It's delocalized all over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So there's no question that the leadership of the company believes that this was a very worthwhile investment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And what that means is that it's there for the long run.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Right. So there is, if you want to talk in these terms, which I don't like, there's a business model, if you want, where FAIR, despite being a very fundamental research lab, brings a lot of value to the company, either mostly indirectly through other sources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Mostly indirectly through other groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now what happened three and a half years ago when I stepped down was also the creation of Facebook AI, which was basically a larger organization that covers FAIR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So FAIR is included in it, but also has other organizations that are focused on applied research or advanced development of AI technology that is more focused on the products of the company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Less emphasis on fundamental research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Less fundamental, but it's still a research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, there's a lot of papers coming out of those organizations and people are awesome and wonderful to interact with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But it serves as kind of a way to kind of scale up, if you want, sort of AI technology, which may be very experimental and sort of lab prototypes into things that are usable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So if you have a subset of meta AI, if FAIR becomes like KFC, it'll just keep the F. Nobody cares what the F stands for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: We'll know soon enough, probably by the end of 2021.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I guess it's not a giant change, FAIR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Well, FAIR doesn't sound too good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But the brand people are kind of deciding on this and they've been hesitating for a while now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: They tell us they're going to come up with an answer as to whether FAIR is going to change name or whether we're going to change just the meaning of the F.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That's a good call. I would keep FAIR and change the meaning of the F.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That would be my preference. I would turn the F into fundamental.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Oh, that's good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Fundamental AI research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Oh, that's really good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Within meta AI. So this would be sort of meta FAIR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But people would call it FAIR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, exactly. I like it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Meta AI is part of the Reality Lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Meta now, the new Facebook is called Meta and it's kind of divided into Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Reality Lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Reality Lab is about AR, VR, telepresence, communication technology and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You can think of it as the sort of a combination of sort of new products and technology part of Meta.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Is that where the touch sensing for robots I saw that you were posting about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Touch sensing for robots is part of FAIR, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Oh, it is? Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah. There is the other way, the haptic glove.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yes, that's more Reality Lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That's Reality Lab research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Reality Lab research. By the way, the touch sensors are super interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Like integrating that modality into the whole sensing suite is very interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So what do you think about the metaverse? What do you think about this whole kind of expansion of the view of the role of Facebook and Meta in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Metaverse really should be thought of as the next step in the internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Sort of trying to make the experience more compelling of being connected either with other people or with content.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And we are evolved and trying to evolve in 3D environments where we can see other people, we can talk to them when we're near them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Or other people are far away and can't hear us. Things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So there are a lot of social conventions that exist in the real world that we can try to transpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now, how compelling is it going to be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Is it going to be the case that people are going to be willing to do this if they have to wear a huge pair of goggles all day? Maybe not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But then again, if the experience is sufficiently compelling, maybe so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Or if the device that you have to wear is just basically a pair of glasses, technology makes sufficient progress for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: AR is a much easier concept to grasp that you're going to have augmented reality glasses that basically contain some sort of virtual assistant that can help you in your daily lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But at the same time with AR, you have to contend with reality. With VR, you can completely detach yourself from reality, so it gives you freedom. It might be easier to design worlds in VR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, but you can imagine the metaverse being a mix.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Or you can have objects that exist in the metaverse that pop up on top of the real world or only exist in virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: OK, let me ask the hard question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because all of this was easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: The Facebook, now Meta, the social network has been painted by the media as negative for society, even destructive and evil at times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You've pushed back against this, defending Facebook. Can you explain your defense?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, so the description, the company that is being described in some media is not the company we know when we work inside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it could be claimed that a lot of employees are uninformed about what really goes on in the company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But I'm a vice president. I mean, I have a pretty good vision of what goes on. I don't know everything, obviously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I'm not involved in everything, but certainly not in decision about content moderation or anything like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But I have some decent vision of what goes on. And this evil that is being described, I just don't see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And then I think there is an easy story to buy, which is that all the bad things in the world and the reason your friends believe crazy stuff,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: there's an easy scapegoat in social media in general, Facebook in particular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: We have to look at the data. Is it the case that Facebook, for example, polarizes people politically?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Are there academic studies that show this? Is it the case that teenagers think of themselves less if they use Instagram more?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Is it the case that people get more riled up against opposite sides in a debate or political opinion if they are more on Facebook or if they are less?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And study after study show that none of this is true. This is independent studies by academics. They're not funded by Facebook or Meta.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: They're studied by Stanford, by some of my colleagues at NYU actually with whom I have no connection. There's a study recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: They paid people, I think it was in the former Yugoslavia, I'm not exactly sure in what part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: but they paid people to not use Facebook for a while in the period before the anniversary of the Sibirnice massacres.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So people get riled up like should we have a memorial kind of celebration for it or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So they paid a bunch of people to not use Facebook for a few weeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It turns out that those people ended up being more polarized than they were at the beginning and the people who were more on Facebook were less polarized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: There's a study from Stanford of economists at Stanford that tried to identify the causes of increasing polarization in the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's been going on for 40 years before Mark Zuckerberg was born continuously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And so if there is a cause, it's not Facebook or social media. So you could say social media just accelerated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But no, I mean, it's basically a continuous evolution by some measure of polarization in the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And then you compare this with other countries like the west half of Germany,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: because you can go 40 years in the East side or Denmark or other countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And they use Facebook just as much. And they're not getting more polarized, they're getting less polarized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So if you want to look for a causal relationship there, you can find a scapegoat, but you can't find a cause.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now, if you want to fix the problem, you have to find the right cause. And what rise me up is that people now are accusing Facebook of bad deeds that are done by others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And those others are we're not doing anything about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And by the way, those others include the owner of the Wall Street Journal, in which all of those papers were published.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So I should mention that I'm talking to Shrep, Mike Shrep on this podcast and also Mark Zuckerberg and probably these conversations can have with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because it's very interesting to me, even if Facebook has some measurable negative effect, you can't just consider that in isolation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You have to consider about all the positive ways it connects us. So like every technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It connects people. It's a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You can't just say like there's an increase in division. Yes, probably Google search engine has created increase in division.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: We have to consider about how much information are brought to the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Like I'm sure Wikipedia created more division if you just look at the division, we have to look at the full context of the world and they didn't make a better world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: The printing press has created more. Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So, you know, when the printing press was invented, the first books that were that were printed were things like the Bible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And that allowed people to read the Bible by themselves, not get the message uniquely from priests in Europe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And that created the protestant movement and 200 years of religious persecution and wars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So that's a bad side effect of the printing press.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You know, social networks aren't being nearly as bad as the printing press, but nobody would say the printing press was a bad idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, a lot of this perception and there's a lot of different incentives operating here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Maybe a quick comment. Since you're one of the top leaders at Facebook and at Meta, sorry, that's in the tech space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I'm sure Facebook involves a lot of incredible technological challenges that need to be solved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: A lot of it probably is in the computer infrastructure, the hardware, the I mean, it's just a huge amount.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Maybe can you give me context about how much of Shrep's life is AI and how much of it is low level compute?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: How much of it is flying all around doing business stuff in the same way as Zuckerberg, Mark Zuckerberg?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: They really focus on AI. I mean, certainly in the run up of the creation of FAIR and for at least a year after that, if not more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Mark was very, very much focused on AI and was spending quite a lot of effort on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And that's his style. When he gets interested in something, he reads everything about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: He read some of my papers, for example, before I joined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And so he learned a lot about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: That'd be great if he said he liked notes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Right. And Shrep was really into it also.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, Shrep is really kind of, has something I've tried to preserve also despite my not so young age,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: which is a sense of wonder about science and technology. And he certainly has that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: He's also a wonderful person in terms of as a manager, dealing with people and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Mark also, actually. I mean, they're very human people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: In the case of Mark, it's shockingly human given his trajectory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I mean, the personality of him that is painted in the press is just completely wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But you have to know how to play the press. So I put some of that responsibility on him too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You have to, it's like the director, the conductor of an orchestra.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You have to play the press in a certain kind of way where you convey your true self to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: If there is a depth and kindness to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It's hard. And he's probably not the best at it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You have to learn. And it's sad to see, I'll talk to him about it, but Shrep is slowly stepping down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It's always sad to see folks sort of be there for a long time and slowly. I guess time is sad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I think he's done the thing he set out to do. And he's got family priorities and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And I understand after 13 years or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It's been a good run.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Which in Silicon Valley is basically a lifetime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Because it's dog years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So NeurIPS, the conference just wrapped up. Let me just go back to something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You posted a paper you co-authored was rejected from NeurIPS, as you said, proudly in quotes, rejected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Can you describe this paper? What was the idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And also maybe this is a good opportunity to ask what are the pros and cons, what works and what doesn't about the review process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Yeah, let me talk about the paper first. I'll talk about the review process afterwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: The paper is called VicReg. So I mentioned that before. Variance, invariance, covariance, regularization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's a technique, a non-contrastive learning technique for what I call joint embedding architecture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So Siamese nets are an example of joint embedding architecture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So joint embedding architecture is... let me back up a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So if you want to do self-supervised learning, you can do it by prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So let's say you want to train a system to predict video.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You show it a video clip and you train the system to predict the next, the continuation of that video clip.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now, because you need to handle uncertainty, because there are many continuations that are plausible, you need to handle this in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You need to have a way for the system to be able to produce multiple predictions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And the only way I know to do this is through what's called a latent variable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So you have some sort of hidden vector of a variable that you can vary over a set or draw from a distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And as you vary this vector over a set, the output, the prediction varies over a set of plausible predictions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So that's called, I call this a generative latent variable model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Now there is an alternative to this, to handle uncertainty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And instead of directly predicting the next frames of the clip, you also run those through another neural net.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So you now have two neural nets, one that looks at the initial segment of the video clip and another one that looks at the continuation during training.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And what you're trying to do is learn a representation of those two video clips that is maximally informative about the video clips themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But it's such that you can predict the representation of the second video clip from the representation of the first one easily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And you can sort of formalize this in terms of maximizing mutual information and some stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But it doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: What you want is informative representations of the two video clips that are mutually predictable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: What that means is that there's a lot of details in the second video clip that are irrelevant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Let's say a video clip consists in a camera panning the scene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: There's going to be a piece of that room that is going to be revealed and I can somewhat predict what that room is going to look like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: But I may not be able to predict the details of the texture of the ground and where the tiles are ending and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So those are irrelevant details that perhaps my representation will eliminate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And so what I need is to train this second neural net in such a way that whenever the continuation video clip varies over all the plausible continuations, the representation doesn't change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Got it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So it's the yeah, got it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Over the space of representations, doing the same kind of thing as you do with similarity learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So these are two ways to handle multimodality in a prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: In the first way, you parameterize the prediction with a latent variable, but you predict pixels essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: In the second one, you don't predict pixels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: You predict an abstract representation of pixels and you guarantee that this abstract representation has as much information as possible about the input, but sort of drops all the stuff that you really can't predict essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I used to be a big fan of the first approach. And in fact, in this paper with the Chan Mishra, this blog post, the Dark Matter Intelligence, I was kind of advocating for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And in the last year and a half, I've completely changed my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I'm now a big fan of the second one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And it's because of a small collection of algorithms that have been proposed over the last year and a half or so, two years, to do this, including V-CRAG, its predecessor called Barlow-Twins, which I mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And a method from our friends at DeepMind could be BYOL.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And there's a bunch of others now that kind of work similarly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So they're all based on this idea of joint embedding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Some of them have an explicit criterion that is an approximation of mutual information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Some others at BYOL work, but we don't really know why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: And there's been like lots of theoretical papers about why BYOL works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: No, it's not that because we take it out and it still works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So there's like a big debate. But the important point is that we now have a collection of non-contrastive joint embedding methods, which I think is the best thing since sliced bread.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: So I'm super excited about this because I think it's our best shot for techniques that would allow us to kind of build predictive models and at the same time, learn hierarchical representations of the world where what matters about the world is preserved and what is irrelevant is eliminated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: By the way, the representations of before and after is in the space in a sequence of images or is it for single images?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: It would be either for a single image for a sequence. It doesn't have to be images. This could be applied to text. This could be applied to just about any signal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: I'm looking for methods that are generally applicable that are not specific to one particular modality. It could be audio or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258

body.input: Got it. So what's the story behind this paper? This paper is describing one such method?

metadata.title: Podcast: Yann LeCun: Dark Matter of Intelligence and Self-Supervised Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #258
